空间: around, round, about

9.22 around 和 round 指围绕的位置或指物体的运动：

We were sitting (a)round the campfire.
The spaceship is travelling (a)round the globe.

about 和 around 常具有“在某一范围里”(in the area of)或“在……里面的不同部位中”(in various positions in)这一模糊含义：

The guests were standing about/around the room.

There are very few taxis about/around here.

在美国英语中，about 用于这一含义的情形比 around 更罕见，也更正式。大体上在美国英语用 around 的场合，英国英语常用 about 或 round.

相对位置还可由通常表示“通过”或“路线”(参见9.25f)的介词表达出来，例如：

The tree lay across the road.
The road runs through the tunnel.

【注】

兰开斯特—奥斯陆/卑尔根和布朗大学书刊英语语料库中，around 和 round 的频率列表如下(包括各种用法)：

<div style="text-align: center;"><div style="text-align: center;">表 9.22 around 和 round 的频率</div> </div>




<table border=1 style='margin: auto; word-wrap: break-word;'><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'></td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>总数</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>〈英国英语〉</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>〈美国英语〉</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>around</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>806</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>245</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>561</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>round</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>410</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>336</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>74</td></tr></table>

##### 相对目的地：over, under, behind 等

9.23 9.19ff 所列的介词（但 above 和 below 通常除外）既表示相对位置，又可表示相对目的地：

He threw a blanket over her.

The bush was the only conceivable hiding place, so I dashed behind it.
When it started to rain, we all went underneath the trees.
这种用法不同于表示从上面、从下面、从后面等通过(passage)的用法(参见9.24)。

##### 通过：over, under, behind 等

9.24 介词和移动动词(verbs of motion)连用，既可表示目的地等的概念，又可表示通过（即向某处移动，然后离开）的概念。9.19 所列介词在下面例[1—3]这一类句子中有上述两种含义：

He jumped over a ditch. [1]
Someone ran behind the goalposts. [2]
The ball rolled underneath the table. [3]

像例[2]和例[3]这类句子，在意义上是模棱两可的。在例[3]中，我们既可说它是表示“通过”的意思(=“the ball passed under the table on the way to some other destination”),也可以说它是表示“目的地”的意思(=“the ball rolled under the table and stayed there”).

【注】

上列例句实际上有三种可能的解释，这在下面的例句中或许看得更清

楚些：

A mouse scuttled behind the curtain.

这句话不仅可以用“通过”或“目的地”的含义来解释，而且可以（稍欠妥）用静态含义来解释，即老鼠一直在帘子后面（来回地窜）。

##### 通过：across, through, past

9.25 across（度1型或2型），through（度2型或3型）和 past（是by 表示“通过”意义的等同词，但它用于这个意思时也可由 by 代替），这三个介词表示方位含义时，主要是指“通过”的意思。注意图9.25中 across 与 on，through 与 in 的比较：

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://pplines-online.bj.bcebos.com/deploy/official/paddleocr/pp-ocr-vl-16-online//c3a88566-d12d-4209-abf7-d91ed1e4245d/markdown_2/imgs/img_in_image_box_124_380_633_516.jpg?authorization=bce-auth-v1%2FALTAKDN8mY5KlNI7zaRpLmOqrw%2F2026-11-03T02%3A20%3A33Z%2F-1%2F%2F108c055cdc660e0b91deb6fba2677c20b4ac2d394489fdbccd920ef842f67888" alt="Image" width="67%" /></div>


<div style="text-align: center;"><div style="text-align: center;">度1型或2型</div> </div>


<div style="text-align: center;"><div style="text-align: center;">图 9.25 on 与 across, in 与 through</div> </div>


图中上面的一对把草看作一个面，因而使人联想起短草；下面的一对把草看作一个立体，使人联想起它有长度、宽度和高度，也就是说草长得很长。在这一点上，over 与 across 的意思相同：

 $$ \mathrm{T h e~b a l l~r o l l e d}\begin{cases}{o v e r}\\ {a c r o s s}\end{cases}{t h e~l a w n}. $$ 

##### 定向路线移动：up，down，along. across 等

9.26 和移动动词连用的 up, down, along, across（与9.25的含义稍有不同）与(a)round 构成一组表示轴线移动或定向路线移动的介词，如图9.26a和9.26b所示：

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://pplines-online.bj.bcebos.com/deploy/official/paddleocr/pp-ocr-vl-16-online//c3a88566-d12d-4209-abf7-d91ed1e4245d/markdown_2/imgs/img_in_image_box_141_824_266_948.jpg?authorization=bce-auth-v1%2FALTAKDN8mY5KlNI7zaRpLmOqrw%2F2026-11-03T02%3A20%3A33Z%2F-1%2F%2F4ab5a2737d07f6b56d7d9126df9b197161f8b8ab5de2ab9b12ff635f1fa67f0f" alt="Image" width="16%" /></div>


<div style="text-align: center;"><div style="text-align: center;">图 9.26a up 与 down</div> </div>


<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://pplines-online.bj.bcebos.com/deploy/official/paddleocr/pp-ocr-vl-16-online//c3a88566-d12d-4209-abf7-d91ed1e4245d/markdown_2/imgs/img_in_image_box_382_826_659_949.jpg?authorization=bce-auth-v1%2FALTAKDN8mY5KlNI7zaRpLmOqrw%2F2026-11-03T02%3A20%3A33Z%2F-1%2F%2F0b5a4afaf5b17f1265a011df619953a9810e6c1907a07a947e878f0244cbf275" alt="Image" width="36%" /></div>


<div style="text-align: center;"><div style="text-align: center;">图 9.26b along 与 across</div> </div>


up 和 down 在垂直方向上相对立，例如：

We walked up the hill and down the other side.
但是在习惯用语中，up 和 down 也用于指水平轴线：
I walked up and down the platform.
She went up/down the road.
up and down 在这里表示“along”(沿着)的意思，不需要有任何垂直的含义(参见19.32)。
along 表示“从一端向另一端”(from one end towards the other) 或“在一条与……平行的线上”(in a line parallel with), 例如：
We walked along the streets, just looking at people.
I took my dog for a walk along the river.
along 与 across [“from one side to another”] 在水平轴线上相对立：
Be careful when you walk across a street.
用(a) round 时，定向路线是有拐角或弧度的：
We ran (a) round the corner.
towards 表示“朝……方向”(in the direction of) 的“实际的”和“隐含的”两种移动：
We walked towards the old farmhouse.
The window faces towards the south.
“隐含的”移动这一概念也解释了其他介词如 to, over 和 into 的用法：
Is this the bus to Oxford?
She glanced over her shoulder.
He spoke into the microphone.
【注】
关于副词(walk) home/homeward(s) 等与上述某些介词短语相对应的问题，参见7.46。

方位：beyond, over, past, up, across 等

9.27 大多数表示相对目的地、通过和定向路线移动(参见9.26)的介词可用来表示静态方位含义。这样，除了两个物体在空间相互联系外，还带来了第三个因素，即“方位点”(POINT OF ORIENTATION)，说话人就站在这一(实际的或想象的)点上。

beyond ["on the far side of"] 这个介词的主要含义是指方位 over, past, across 和 through 这几个介词则把 "beyond" 的含义同 9.26 中所描述的关于度的更加具体的情况结合起来了：

They live across the moors.[即“from here”]

The village is  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} past the bus stop. \\ through the wood. \end{array}\right. $

up, down, along 和(a)round 在下例中用来指轴线的方位：
the shop down the road ["towards the bottom end of..."]

Her office is  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}up the stairs. \quad\left[\text{“at(或 towards) the top of...”}=\text{upstairs} \\\text{down the stairs.}\quad\left[\text{“at(或 towards) the bottom of...”}=\text{downstairs}\end{array}\right.\end{array}\right. $

There's a hotel across/along the road. ["on the other side/towards the other end of..."]

假如我们愿意的话，可以用 from-短语表明方位点。

He lives up/down/along/across the road from me.

##### 结果含义：from, out of, over, past 等

9.28 具有移动含义的介词(如例[1])与动词连用时，通常也可以有静态的结果含义，表示“已经到达目的地的状态”，如在例[2]中(参见8.42)：

The horses jumped over the fence.

The horses are over the fence. ["have now jumped over"]

如果离开上下文，结果含义往往不能和其他静态含义区别开来。然而，它的存在经常可以通过某些副词(already, just, at last, (not) yet 等)表示出来。我们还发现否定介词(from, out of 等)或“通过”介词(如 across, through, past)常具有这种结果含义：

At last we are out of the forest. [3]

When you're past the next obstacle, you can relax. [4]

##### 遍及含义(pervasive meaning): over, throughout, with 等

9.29 over（度1型或度2型）与 through（度2型或度3型）具有遍及含义（静态的或移动的），尤其是它们的前面出现 all 时：

That child was running (all) over the flower borders throughout 的含义是 (all) through，唯有这个介词的主要含义是“遍及”：

Chaos reigned (all) through the house.

The epidemic has spread throughout the country. 偶尔9.26中的“轴线”型介词也用来表示遍及的意思：

There were crowds (all) along the route.

They put flowers (all) around the statue.

with 在以下一类词组中也具有遍及含义：

The ground was covered with snow.

The garden was buzzing with bees.

类似的例子还有：loaded with, paved with, surrounded with, dotted with 等。

##### over 的八种意义

9.30 现在我们来观察一个介词（over）用来表达不同意义的情况：

位置(9.19): A lamp hung over the door.

目的地(9.23): They threw a blanket over her.

通过(9.24): They climbed over the wall.

方位(9.27): They live over the road. ["on the far side of"]

结果(9.28): At last we were over the crest of the hill.

遍及[静态的](9.29): Leaves lay thick (all) over the ground.

遍及[移动](9.29): They splashed water (all) over me.

伴随情况： We discussed it over a glass of wine.

##### 包含介词含义的动词

9.31 当一个动词本身的含义中包括了后随介词的含义时，常有可能将这个介词省略；这时动词变成及物动词，介词补足语变成直接位置宾语（参见10.27）。下面的例子主要表示空间含义，但也有一些其他例子说明这一变化过程并不限于介词的空间用法：

roam (about/around) the city ponder (on) a question pass (by) a house turn (round) a corner flee (from) the country attain (to) a position cross (over) a street climb (up) a mountain jump/leap (over) a fence pierce (through) the defences

在许多情况下，这两种结构有意义上的差别。带介词的结构注重于过程(process)，而直接宾语结构却具有完成含义，表示目标已经达到。试比较：

Let's swim across the river.
She was the first woman to swim the Channel.

##### 地点介词的比喻用法或抽象用法

9.32 许多地点介词具有抽象意义，这些抽象意义通过比喻的手法与地点介词的位置用法明显地联系起来。介词的这种抽象用法常常保留它们本来表示地点时的搭配形式（根据意思的相似或差异）。表示时间的介词也常有这种用法（参见 9.33ff）。

我们从(a)至(d)几组介词短语可以看出地点介词的比喻用法在逐步引申：

(a) in shallow water [纯粹按字面意思解释]
(b) in deep water [也可用作比喻，“in trouble”]
(c) in difficulties [名词不是比喻用法，而介词却是]

(d) in a tough spot ["in a difficult situation"; 这个短语中的介词与(c)中的介词相似，但名词又用了一个位置比喻，结果就形成了一个不能按字面意思解释的短语，因为如果按照字面意思，spot 之前应该用 at 或 on(度0型)。]

和字面意思相关的例子有：
in/out of; amid, amidst〈都属正式用法，且罕见〉(参见 9.21【注】
[a])

in/out of; amid, amidst<都属正式用法，且罕见>（参见 9.21 [a])
位置→状态，情况：
to be in/out of danger to keep out of trouble
to be in/out of office to be out of a job
to be in difficulties amidst many troubles
包含存在……之内→抽象的包含：
in books/plays in/out of the race
in a group/party
into/out of
目的地→抽象的情况或环境：
He got into difficulties/trouble/debt/a fight.
Can you get me out of this mess?
in/on
位置→成员资格，参与：
in the army
on the board/committee/project
above/below/beneath
垂直方向→抽象的水平：
to be above/below someone on a list
above/below[不说：*beneath] one's income
Such behaviour is beneath [不说：*below] him.
He's above[不说：*over] such behaviour.
above (the) average
above suspicion
under
垂直方向→遭受，从属；过程：
under suspicion/orders/compulsion
He has a hundred people working under him.
The bridge is under construction.
up/down
在垂直轴线上移动→名次或度数、等级上变动位置：
move up/down the scale

climb up/down the social ladder
from/to
出发点/目的地→始发者/接受者：
a letter/present from Browning to his wife (参见9.46f)
beyond/past/over

结果含义；有形的→抽象的：

beyond} {belief
    endurance
    past} hope
    recovery

We are over the worst.
between/among/amongst(参见9.21【注】【a]）
相对位置→参与者之间的抽象关系：
a fight/match between X and Y
We quarrel/agree among ourselves.
relationship/contrast/affinity between two thing
through
通过→坚韧不拔，忍耐
She came through the ordeal.
We put him through his paces.
We are through the worst.

##### 【注】

[a] over 和 under 在度量词组 [expressions of measure) 中作“强化介词”(intensifying preposition) 时，意思是“more than”或“less than”(参见 7.87ff 中的强化语)：
The car was travelling (at)  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} over \\ under \end{array}\right\} $ sixty miles per hour.
试比较：overage; overconfident ["overly confident"]
above 和 below 也可以用于表示温度：
The temperature is  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} above/over \\ below/under \end{array}\right\} $ 30°.
但是，在与 zero degrees 连用时仅用下列介词：

above/below zero.

[b] 有几个介词(主要是 in 和 out of)可用于明显相反的关系中，如：The horse is in foal. ["There is a foal in the horse's womb."]
The office is out of envelopes. ["There are no envelopes in the office."]
We are in luck/out of luck.

[c] 不定式标记由于比喻关系可以看作与空间介词相关联。试比较下列各组：

John went
{
to the pool. [方向：“Where did he go?”]
to the pool for a swim. [方向+目的：“Why did he go to the pool?”]
for a swim in the pool. [目的+位置]
for a swim. [目的：“Why did he go there?”]
to swim. [不定式标记的“比喻关系”(在to-不定式分句中)]
swimming. [非限定性动词分句]

##### 表示时间的介词

9.33 时间介词短语通常以附加状语 (He came on Friday) 后置修饰语 (the party on Friday)，或谓体附加状语 (That was on Friday) 出现；但有时它也可能本身就是时间介词的补语 (参见 9.1 【注】[d]):

a voice from out of the past

介词的时间用法常常表示从地点范围作比喻性引申，类似9.32所讨论的种种引申转义。

时间位置：at, on, in, by

9.34 at, on 和 in 作“时间位置”介词时，在某种程度上与它们作肯定位置介词（参见 9.16）时分别对等，但在时间范围内只有两种“度型”，即“时间点”和“时间段”(参见 8.51ff):

at 用来指时间点（主要指钟点，[例1]），习惯上也用来指假日时节如例[2]：

at ten o'clock, at 6.30 p.m., at noon [1] at the weekend〈英国英语；但在美国英语里：on the weekend〉, at Christmas, at Easter [2]

at Christmas 和 at Easter 是指整个圣诞节或复活节这种时节，而不是只指这一天本身。at 也可以用来表示作时间点考虑的时间段，如：

at the/that time, at breakfast time, at night
on 用来指当作时间段看待的一天：
on Monday, on the following day, on May (the) first,
on New Year's Day

on 还出现在下面的词组中：

Trains leave the station on the hour. ["hourly", 即 1 o'clock, 2 o'clock 等]
in 或(用得较少的) during 表示比一天更长或更短的一段时间：
in the evening in summer
in August during Holy Week
in 1969 in the eighteenth century
in the months that followed

following evening 等表明，on 加了一个补足语后有一种特殊用法，即指一天的一部分，而不是指全天。这种用法也扩展到其他一些情况，其中的一段时间是指实际提到的某一天的一部分：on the morning of 1 June 等。但在 early morning，late afternoon 这样的短语之前，通常用 in，如 in the late afternoon。

指夜晚的一段时间时，我们用 in，试比较：

I woke up several times in the night.
At night I usually have the window open. ["during the night"; 与 in the evening, in the day 相对立]
by 出现在习语 by day 和 by night 中，分别代替 during the day / the night，与某些活动（例如旅行）连用：

We preferred travelling  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} by night. \\ during the night. \end{array}\right. $
We stayed up during the night.

将来时间的衡量：in

9.35 后置副词 ago 用来衡量从现在起回溯到过去某一点时间之间的一段时间，而 in 则用来表示从现在起展望到将来与上述相同的一段时间(参见 8.58f):

We met three months ago. [1]
We'll meet  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}in three months' time. \quad [2] \ $ in) three months from now. \quad [3]\end{array}\right. $

例 $$ 2—3 $$ 中的结构只有在表示“at the end of a period of three months starting from now”这一意思时才能成立。要从过去某一点时间向前衡量时，只有下面的结构才是常用的：

He finished the job { in three months.["in the space of three months from when he started it"] [4] ?(in) three months from then. [5] *in three months' time. [6]

持续: for, during, over, (all) through, throughout

9.36 持续时间短语回答“时间多长？”的问题。持续的含义通常由 for 来表示。试比较持续和时间位置：

A: How long did you camp in Scotland?
B: We camped there for the summer. ["all through, from the beginning to the end of the summer"]
A: When did you camp in Scotland?
B: We camped there in the summer. ["at some time during the summer"]

持续短语 for the summer 表示逗留时间持续了整整一个夏季；时间 -when 短语 in the summer 则表示逗留时间包含 (included) 在夏季之中。during the summer 在这里可以与 in 表达同样的含义，尽管 during 通常是表示持续的：

We managed to stay awake during the whole meeting. 如果没有 stay 和 whole 这一类持续标记，during 指的是持续时间范围以内的一个时间点或时间段而不是指持续时间本身：

She spoke during the meeting.

During our  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} stay\ in\\ visit\ to\end{array}\right\} $ Japan we met several old friends.

for 也用于 forever，for good ["forever"], for years (and years)这类习月短语中。

over, (all) through 和 throughout 具有持续时间的含义，和它们表示地点的遍及含义相对应(参见 9.29)。

We camped there over the holiday/over Christmas/over the weekend/over the Sabbath/over night. We camped there through(out) the summer.

over 通常和表示特殊日子(例如假日和节日)的名词短语搭配，因而所指的时间一般比 through(out)所指的更短。由于星期六(Saturday)和星期日(Sunday)比一周的其他日子“特殊”些，所以我们用 over Saturday and Sunday，通常不用 over Wednesday. over the last three years, over the last generation 这类词组似乎已变得越来越常用了。

【注】

for 在下面两个句子中有不同含义：

I've done that for years.
I've not done that for years.

在肯定句例[1]中，行动包含在 for 所表示的一段时间中，即属于内包持续时间（included duration）。另一方面，在否定句例[2]中，行动被排除在 for 所表示的一段时间之外，即属于外排持续时间（excluded duration）（“It's years since I've done that”，“I haven't done that in years”）。这里要注意 in〈尤其在美国英语中〉只能用于否定句：

 $$ \mathrm{~I~}\left\{\substack{h a v e n^{\prime}t}{*h a v e}\right\}\mathrm{d o n e~t h a t~i n~y e a r s}. $$ 

持续：from...to, until, up to

9.37 from...to（或 till）是另一对把位置含义转为时间持续含义的介词。美国英语选用（from）...through 这一词组，以避免在 through 后面提到的时间是否包括在整段时间之内这一问题上的含混不清。（参见 between...and，9.39；另外再参见“前跨”；8.58f）：

We camped there (from) June through September.〈美

国英语>
["up to and including September"]
We camped there from June  $ \left\{\begin{matrix} \text{to} \\ \text{till} \end{matrix}\right\} $ September.
["up to (?and including) September"]
但是，如果没有 from 一词，就只能用 until，till，up to（但不能总是仅仅用 to）和 through〈美国英语〉：

We camped there  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} until \\ till \\ up to \\ through\langle 美国英语 \rangle \\ *to \end{array}\right\} $ September.

另一方面，to 可以与 till 换用，如：

You can stay to/till the end of September.
The meeting can be postponed to/till September.
There are only a few days to/till September.
I have only a few years to/till retirement.

from 和 up to 分别表示一段时间的起点和终点。up to 通常表明一段较长的时间，其中不包括介词补足语中所述的那一段时间：

From 1982 (onwards) the rules were changed. We worked up to Christmas. (但不包括 Christmas 在内)

在非正式用法中，有时 up 出现在 until 和 till 之前：

I worked (up)  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} until \\ till \\ to \end{array}\right\} $ last week.

till 和 until 只能与持续动词(durative verbs)，即表示一段时间动词(如 camp 和 work)连用。试对照：

My girlfriend {worked} there till Christmas.
所以，until 与 till 的情况与 by 相反，by 表示终点(end point)，只与瞬时动词(momentary verbs)连用(参见9.39):

She  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} \text{worked} \\ \text{arrived} \end{array}\right\} $ by Christmas.

在否定的语境中，until 和 till 不论与持续动词还是与瞬时动词连用都是成立的：

She didn't arrive there till Christmas.

然而，till 与 until 与肯定谓体(positive predication)和否定谓体(negative predication)连用时，有两种不同的含义。与肯定谓体连用时，till 与 until/表示时间终点("up to");而与否定谓体连用时，它们表示的却是时间起点("before"):

We slept until midnight. ["We stopped sleeping then."] We didn't sleep until midnight. ["We started sleeping then."]

##### before, after, since, till, until

9.38 这些词既是介词又是连接词（参见14.12ff）。它们作介词时，几乎毫无例外地是时间介词，后面或者接：

(a) 时间名词短语(after next week);

(b) 无主语-ing 分句(since leaving school); 或者接

(c) (带有从动词派生的名词的)名词短语(参见附录 I.34f)，或接视为相当于分句的其他名词短语：

before the war ["before the war started or took place"] till/until the fall of Rome ["until Rome fell"] since electricity ["since electricity was invented"]

我们用 for 表示(在 since 所指的起点时间之后)持续的一段时间(参见 9.36)

We have lived in New York  $ {^{since}} $ 1980. for 4 years.
We lived in Chicago for 15 years.

关于带 since 分句的动词形式，参见 14.26。

before 和 after 表示两个时间或两个事件的关系，这两个词的词义相反(参见9.19,9.35ff):

{The meeting will take place after the ceremony.
=The ceremony will take place before the meeting.

##### 【注】

The decision must wait pending his trial. ["until"] Pending negotiations, the two parties should stop further action. ["during and till the end of"] 所以，pending也能包括“during”的含义。

between...and, by

9.39 between...and 表示在由起点和终点指明的一段时间之中，但与from...to（参见9.37）不同，它并不表示动词在整个这一段时间的延续：

We'll probably arrive some time between 5 and 6 o'clock. I'll phone you between lunch and dinner.
between X and Y 可以包含 X 和 Y 在内，如：

I'll ring between Thursday and Saturday.

这个词组并不意味着将要在星期五打电话，也有可能在星期四或星期六打。所以，between...and的意思是“about”，即“some time on Thursday，Friday，or Saturday”。between还用来表示重复出现的相同事物之间的间隔：

between meals/dances/acis/classes
by 表示一件事情出现结果的那一点时间：
Your papers are to be handed in by next week. ["not later than"]
She should be back by now. [可我没有把握]
by 表示时间的终点。它在含义上和 already, still, yet 和 any more 有联系：
By the time we'd walked five miles, he was already exhausted.
试对照：
By that time he was already exhausted. ["He was then exhausted."]
Until then he was not exhausted. ["Before then he was not exhausted."]

所以，by-短语不与持续动词连用(参见 9.37):

The troops remained there  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} ^{until} \\  by \end{array}\right\} $ midnight.

【注】

与地点介词(参见9.32)一样，时间介词和时间介词副词也可以有比喻用法，例如将人生看作旅途：

At birth...from the age of two... reaching the age of 16, he left school days behind, and adulthood was in front of him...all through middle age...up to 1945.

在表示时间的词组中适宜不用介词的情况

9.40 在许多情况下，时间介词不出现，因此时间状语以名词短语的形式而不是以介词短语的形式出现。

紧接在指示词(deictic words) last, next, this, that 和量词 some 和 every 之前的时间 when-介词总是省略：

I saw her  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} last\ Thursday. \\ *on\ last\ Thursday. \end{array}\right. $
I'll mention it next time I see her.
This year, plums are more plentiful than last.
Some day you'll regret this decision.
Every summer she returns to her childhood home.

词义中含有“last”，“next”或“this”意义的名词之前也不用时间介词：

I saw her  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} today. \\ yesterday \ (morning). \end{array}\right\} $ I'll see her tomorrow (evening).

在时间词组中，适宜省略的介词似乎只限于 at，on，in；其他介词，例如 before 和 since，不能省略：

I'll see you  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} on Monday. \\ Monday. \end{array}\right\}= $
before Monday.
Monday
I haven't seen her since last week.

如果指示短语所表示的时间与目前有一定间隔，那末它前面的介词可有可无，例如：

(on) Monday week
(on) the day before yesterday.
{in the January before last〈英国英语〉
the January before last〈美国英语和英国英语〉

有些短语表达的时间是在过去(或将来)某个时间之前或之后，这时介词也是可有可无的：

(in) the previous spring ["the spring before the time in question"]
(at)〈英国英语〉
(on)〈美国英语〉}the following weekend
(on) the next day

因此，有以下可以互相换用的形式：

 $$ \mathrm{~W e~m e t}\begin{cases}{{o n~t h e~f o l l o w i n g~d a y.}}\\ {{t h e~f o l l o w i n g~d a y.}}\\ \end{cases}\mathrm{~W e~m e t}\begin{cases}{{o n~t h a t~d a y.}}\\ {{t h a t~d a y.}}\\ \end{cases} $$ 

总的说来，无介词的句子往往用于不太正式的语体中，也较为常见。

包含 the 并带有后置修饰语的非指示短语在英国英语中常用介词，而在美国英语中介词是可有可无的：

 $$  We~met\begin{cases}on~the~day\\ the~day&of~the~conference.\\ in~the~spring\\ the~spring<尤其美国英语 >\end{cases}\}of~1983。 $$ 

但在没有后置修饰语的情况下，介词总是不可缺少的：

 $$ \mathrm{~W e~m e t~i n~t h e~s p r i n g.}\quad\neq\mathrm{W e~m e t~t h e~s p r i n g}. $$ 

〈在英国英语中〉，下列一类词序(next Sunday, last January) 倒装的短语通常不省略介词：

 $$ \mathrm{(o n)~S u n d a y~n e x t}\quad\mathrm{(i n)~J a n u a r y~l a s t} $$ 

【注】

在一个特定的星期中，假如我们指即将到来的一天的名称，有些人把 next X-day（如 next Friday）用来指“同一星期的某天”，而其他人却用它指“下一星期的某天”。另一方面，this X-day（如：this Friday）却总是指“本星期的某天”。这种情况也适用于月份，如 next September 和 this September.

##### 在频率词组中不用介词的情况

9.41 在如下的频率短语中不用介词，如：

Every Sunday, we usually go for a walk.

如果没有像 every 这种频率标记，介词是可有可无的，而表示周日的

名词可以是单数，也可以是复数。没有介词的结构用于非正式语体〈尤其是美国英语〉：

On Sunday(s)
Sunday(s)
*On every Sunday}we usually go for a walk.
Three times a week
*At three times a week}we play darts.

但其他频率结构却总是要求用介词：

with+形容词+frequency: with regular frequency
at→形容词+intervals: at irregular intervals
on+形容词+occasions: on specific occasions
from time to time: We saw each other from time to time.
at a/the rate of+名词: at the rate of $20 an hour
between/at+each+单数名词 He had dropped the habit of drinking coffee at all hours.
词，或 all+复数名词：

在持续时间词组中不用介词的情况

9.42 for 指的是一段持续的时间。介词 for 在持续时间短语（与静态含义的动词连用）中常常省略：

We stayed there(for) three months.
The snowy weather lasted (for) the whole time we were there.
(For) a lot of the time we just lay on the beach.

在以 all 开头的短语(如 all (the) week, all day) 之前，介词必须省略。但请比较与 all 同义的 whole(参见 5.17):

We stayed there  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} all (the) week. \\ (for) the whole week. \\ *for all week. \end{array}\right. $
I haven't seen her all day.

然而，与动态动词（它的动作显然不是在表明的这一段时间内自始至终延续的）连用时，介词不能省略。试比较：

I lived there  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} \text { for three years, } \\ \text { three years. } \end{array}\right. $
I taught her  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} \text { for three years. } \\ ?* \text { three years. } \end{array}\right. $

类似的例子还有：

I haven't spoken to her  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} for three months. \\ *three months. \end{array}\right. $

介词在分句的开头也不能省略：

(For 600 years, the cross lay undisturbed.
(The cross lay undisturbed (for) 600 years.

同样地，for ages, for days, for years 等短语出现在句首时，介词通常不省略。然而，在时间词组中如用并列连词，会增加可接受的程度。试比较：

(?) Years and yerrs} we have all been expecting this event.

##### 地点和时间以外的意义范围

9.43 现在我们考察介词(除了表示时间和地点以外)更为重要的一些用法。众所周知，将介词的含义分门别类是很困难的。在有些情况下，最好将介词的含义作为一个范围或系列来处理，即首先看作单一的大类，然后再分成若干独立的、互相有所重叠的小类。所以，我们先来探讨两个重要的大类。为了简便起见，不妨把这两大类称为原因(CAUSE)/目的(PURPOSE)系列和手段(MEANS)/施动者(AGENTIVE)系列。我们把各种不同的含义放在同一个标题下面，原因之一是有些作为连接成分与某些特定介词和 wh-词相关联：原因/目的系列与 for，why 和 how 有关；手段/施动者系列与 with 和 how 有关。现将两大系列的各种含义举例说明如下：

原因/目的系列（参见9.44—47）

原因(9.44): She lost her job because of her age.
理由(9.44): He was fined for drunken driving.
动机(9.44): She did it out of kindness.
目的(9.44): Everyone ran for shelter.
目的地(9.45): I'm leaving for Seattle.
目标(9.46): This novel is aimed at a young audience.

手段/施动者系列(9.48—51)

方式(9.48)：She performed the operation with great skill.
手段(9.49)：They left by plane.
工具(9.49)：She tried to open the lock with a knife.
施动者(9.50)：They were noticed by no one.
刺激(9.51)：I'm astonished at your reaction.

##### 原因/目的系列

原因、理由、动机：because of, on account of, for, from 等

9.44 在原因/目的系列的一端，有些介词表示某事发生的物质原因或心理原因(动机)。原因、理由和动机短语是用来回答问句“why…?”的。例如：

We had to drive slowly because of the heavy rain.
On account of his wide experience, he was made chairman.
The survivors were weak from exposure and lack of food.
Some support charities out of duty, some out of a sense of guilt.
I hid the money, for fear of what my parents would say.
The plane was destroyed through the pilot's carelessness.

on account of 表示原因或理由，是 because of 在正式语体中的代替形式。out of 和 for 主要限于表达动机（即心理原因）；out of gratitude/kindness 等。

for 出现在相对来说来数量较小的词组中，如：

for fear/love/joy/sorrow

He offered to fix my sink for  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} nothing. < 非正式用法  \\  free. < 非正式用法, 尤其在美国英语里 \end{array}\right. $

目的、预定目的地：for

9.45 for 在下面的例句中表示目的：

He'll do anything for money.
Everyone ran for shelter.
For the journey, they packed three large picnic baskets of food.

for 的这种用法有一个与之相对应的同义分句 (in order) to (参见 15.48):

for money=in order to gain money
for shelter=in order to reach shelter

for 表示预定目的地 (INTENDED DESTINATION) 时，与 run, start, head, leave 和 set out 等动词连用。例如：
He set out for London.

用 to-短语是假设将会到达目的地。

试比较：

He  $ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} went to \\ left for \end{array} \right\} $ London. Is this the train  $ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} to \\ for \end{array} \right\} $ London?

目的或目的地短语回答“Why...?”，“What...for?”，“Where...for?”或“Who...for?”这类问句。它们用作后置修饰语（例[1]），附加状语（例[2]）和系动词分句中的补语（例[3—4]）：

The scenery for the play is splendid. [1]
She came for the play. [2]
This present is for you. [3]
This machine is for washing dishes. [4]

【注】

注意 for fun 和 in fun 在意义上的差别：
He did it for fun. ["with the object of getting amusement"]
He said it in fun. ["jokingly", "in jest"]

接受者、目的、目标：for，to，at

9.46 当 for 的后面接表示人或动物的名词短语时，多半带有“预定接受者”(INTENDED RECIPIENT)的意味：

He laid a trap for his enemies. [1]

She made a beautiful doll for her daughter.
He cooked a dinner for her.

for-短语表示预定接受者(她女儿或许已经收到洋娃娃，或许还没有)时，常常相当于一个间接宾语(参见10.7,16.56):

She made her daughter a beautiful doll. [2a]
He cooked her a dinner. [3a]

与 for 所表达的预定接受者的概念相对立，to 在句子中表示“实际接受者”(ACTUAL RECIPIENT)，例如：

She gave a beautiful doll to her daughter.

同样地，to 也常与间接宾语的结构相联系：

I  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{gave}\\ \text{lent}\\ \text{sold}\end{array}\right\} $ the book to my friend.
 $ \sim I\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{gave}\\ \text{lent}\\ \text{sold}\end{array}\right\} $ my friend the book.

但也有结构不能转换的情况。例如：

I delivered the book to my friend.
*I delivered my friend the book.

在 aim at 一类的组合(其中介词短语是动词的补语)中，at 表达预定目的或目标：

After aiming carefully at the bird, he missed it completely. [4]
A vicious dog was snapping at her ankles. [5]
She smiled at me. [6]

如例[4]所示，预定目标不一定要达到，at的这种用法和直接宾语之间的差别，可以在许多例子(kick at, charge at, bite at, catch at, shoot at, chew at)中看出来：用at则暗示“希望达到某种目的”，而直接宾语结构表示按计划达到了目的或完成了某个行动。She shot at him与She shot him的意思大不相同：第一句可补充说“but missed him”，而第二句则不能。在其他动词不是及物的情况下，如果要强调达到目的，就必须用to：

She ran at me. [表示敌意：“attacked”]

She ran to me. [表示向某一目标的移动]

类似的有：point at/to, throw at/to

##### 【注】

[a] 和话语动词(如 roar, bellow, shout, mutter, growl) 搭配时，at 和 to 之间有明显区别。例[7]暗示仅仅把我当作一个目标(例如辱骂的对象)，而例[8]则暗示叫喊的人正在和我说话，即我是信息的接受者：
He shouted at me. [7]
He shouted to me. [8]
at 在这里通常含有敌意。同样地，laugh at 表示敌意(例[9])，除非那宾语是有意引人发笑的(如讲笑话)(例[10])：
They first laughed at us. [9]
They laughed heartily at our jokes. [10]
[b] 在 work + 目标的组合中，美国英语用介词 on，英国英语既可用 on 又可用 at:
She is working on her new play.

##### 来源、籍贯：from

来源、籍贯：From
9.47 与 to ("goal") 相反的介词是 from ["source"] (参见 18.31【注】)：
Bill lent the book to me. ~I borrowed the book from Bill.
from 也用来指“籍贯”：
He comes from Scotland/Glasgow. ["He is a Scot/a Glasgowian."]
这类介词短语不仅用作附加状语，还用作系动词分句例[1]的补语和后置修饰语例[2]：
I'm from Madrid. [1]
This is a friend of mine from London. [2]

##### 手段/施动者系列

方式：in...manner, like, with
9.48 in...manner 和 with 可表示方式。例如：

The job was done in a workmanlike manner. We were received with the utmost courtesy.

与及物或不及物动词连用时，like 可包含“以类似……方式”的意思(in a manner resembling)；与系动词连用时，只有“相似”(resemblance)这一含义：

The army swept through the city like a pestilence. Life is like a dream.

在主要动词不是系动词的句子中，外加状语（参见 8.121ff）表示“相似”这种含义是常见的。试对比：

似”这种含义是常见的。试对比：
Bill writes poetry like his  $ BR\dot{O}THER $. ["in a manner resembling that of his brother's poetry"]
Like his  $ BR\dot{O}THER $, Bill writes POETry. [相似]
Bill writes POETry, like his  $ BR\dot{O}THER $.

上面最后一对例句表明，含义上的差别不单纯是词序的安排问题。

unlike 用来表示对相似的否定即 “not like”:
Unlike his brother (who writes poetry), Bill writes science fiction.
Bill writes science fiction, unlike his brother (who writes poetry).

与 like 不同，作介词和连接词用的 as 指实际的身分和地位 (actual role) (参见 9.4):

She spoke  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} like a L\dot{A}Wyer. \quad [“in a manner resembling”] \\ as a L\dot{A}Wyer. \quad [“in that capacity”] \\ as a L\dot{A}Wyer \text{ does.} \quad [“in that manner”] \end{array}\right. $

方式短语（manner phrases）和方式副词经常可以互换：with courtesy ～courteously. 方式短语和方式副词有时都能用问句“How...?”来发问，尤其是语境或动词词义使它们排除掉“手段”的含义时：

A: How did she speak? B: She spoke  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}competently\\with great skill.\end{array}\right. $

A: How did you travel? B:  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} By air. \\ Comfortably. \end{array}\right. $

手段和工具：by，with，without

9.49 手段和工具短语用来回答“How...?”问句。by 能表达“by

means of”(注意冠词的省略；参见5.45)的含义：

I usually go to work by bus/train/car/boat. [mode of transport]
Communication took place by letter/telex/radio/post
〈英国英语〉mail〈美国英语〉. [means of communication]
The thief must have entered and left the house by (=
through) the back door.
By working the pumps, we kept the ship afloat for another 40 hours.

with 则表达工具的含义(instrumental meaning)(参见 9.50):
Someone had broken the window with a stone. [1]
He caught the ball with his left hand. [2]

例句\[1-2](通常要求主语是人，并有一个直接宾语)相当于例句\[1a-

2a] (含有动词 use + 一个带 (in order) to + 动词不定式的短语):
Someone had used a stone to break the window. [1a]
He used his left hand to catch the ball. [2a]

也可用另一种结构来替换，其中表示工具的名词短语变成了主语（关于“工具”主语，参见10.21）；

A stone had broken the window. [1b]
His left hand caught the ball. [2b]

就 with 所表达的大多数含义（包括工具含义）而言，without 是与它相对应的反义词：
I drew it without (using) a ruler. ["I did not draw it with a ruler."]

##### 【注】

[a] 运输方式既可以用 by，又可用 on 来表达，如 on the bus/the train/a ship/a plane。这些并不是纯粹的位置短语（在这种情况下，表示位置用 in，而不是用 on，参见 9.18f)，而是表示正处于“运送”状态之中。试比较例句[3—6]：
I go to work on the bus.
I go to work by bus.
I met Peter on the bus.
*I met Peter by bus

例句[3]没有例句[4]那样常用；但尽管我们可以说例句[5]，却不能说例句[6]。by后面不带修饰语的名词语短通常不用冠词，但并不是说冠词非去掉不可：

It's easier to go to town by the bus (rather than by the train).

在短语 on foot, on horseback 中，用 on 而不用 by。注意这些短语和 by bus 一类短语一样不用冠词(参见 5.45)。by 后面的名词短语，不允许用修饰语，除非加进限定词：

by$\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text { the last, bus } \\\text { the }2\text { o'clock bus } \\\text { *last bus }\end{array}\right.$

[b] of 与动词 die 连用，如 He died of hunger 等。这种含义介于“原因”与“手段”之间：一方面是谈“死因”（试比较：He died from exposure.）；另一方面，这种短语常常是回答问句“How did he die?”（或 What did he die of?），而不是回答问句“Why did he die?”的。

##### 工具和施动者：with，by

我们发现例[1]相当于例[1a]和例[1b]:
Someone used a stone to break the window. [1a]
A stone had broken the window. [1b]

例句[1]还与被动句[1c]相关连：

The window had been broken with a stone by someone [1c]

在被动句中，施动者由 by-短语(参见 3.65)表示：by someone。然而，在大多数被动句中，施动者 by-短语实际上是省略的，如例[1d]：

The window had been broken with a stone. [1d]

在例 $ [1c] $这种被动句中，by-施动者具有施动作用(参见 $ [10.19] $)，相当于主动句(例 $ [1] $)中主语的施动作用。施动者是动作产生的缘由，一般是有生命的(通常是人)，又如：

{A passing stranger observed us. We were observed by a passing stranger.

然而，我们也可以发现无生命的 by-短语，如例[3a]：
{Frost has ruined the crops. [3]
The crops have been ruined by frost. [3a]

在例[1d]这种情况下，工具也可以由 by-短语来表示：
The window had been broken by a stone. [1e]

不论例句[1d]还是例句[1e]，都能描述同一件事，但在含义上可能有
差别，这一点在下面两个句子中表现得更清楚：

My car had been damaged {by the branch of a tree. [4]} with the branch of a tree. [4a]

例[4]中的by排除了将人作为施动者：或许是风暴刮断的树枝使汽车损坏了。相比之下，例[4a]中的with排除了自然原因，并暗示作为施动者的人用了从树上折下的树枝去进行破坏。

由此，我们区分出施动者和工具。施动者是唆使或引起(由动词所表示的)某件事情发生的生物；工具是施动者用来完成某事或唆使某事发生的实体(通常是无生物)。施动者和工具都可说成是表示施动的语义功能的。

by-短语还用作后置修饰语表示作者（参见17.46【注】[c]）：
a picture by Degas ["painted by Degas"] [6]
a novel by Tolstoy ["written by Tolstoy"] [6]
a five-year-old horse by Willwin out of Lady Barle [7]
[一匹马的来源] [7]
through 在以下句子中有“媒介”的含意，如：
They are related through their grandmother.
The presidents had to communicate through an inter-
preter.
through Jesus Christ Our Lord [用作祈祷完毕时的套
语]

##### 【注】

[a] 区分“工具”和“施动者”的原因之一是它们不能并列使用，也不能通过并列，压缩为单一的介词短语(参见13.40)：
 $ ^{*} $He was killed by a man and (by) an arrow.
然而，如果涉及不同的过程，就能并列使用，但会产生类似轭式搭配(zeugma)的效果(参见13.37):

The area was ravaged by floods and by guerilla forces.

[b] 表示施动者和工具的by-短语，除了出现在被动语态的分句中外，还可以出现在被动含义的-ed 分词形容词的后面（参见3.74ff）：I was very alarmed by the news he brought. [8] The child was unwanted by its parents. [9] His services to the community have not gone unnoticed by those who have benefited. [10]

例[8]中的强调成分 very，例[9]和例[10]中的前缀 un-和例[10]中作系动词用的 go（参见16.21）是分词作形容词用的标志（参见7.15ff）。

[c] by-短语既可指“手段”又可指“工具”，如在下面的句子中：

The news was confirmed by a telegram. [或者“Someone confirmed it by means of a telegram.”, 或者“A telegram confirmed it.”].

由于工具的含义是和被动分句联系在一起的，因此主动分句只能表达“手段”含义：

##### 刺激因素：at

9.51 一种情绪和它的刺激物（通常是抽象的刺激因素）之间的关系常常可以用 at 或表示工具的 by 来表达（参见 9.50）：

I was alarmed  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}at\\ by\end{array}\right\} $ his behaviour.

以上句子都可以看作与下句的被动语态句子等同：
His behaviour alarmed me. [fa]

接在 at 后面的名词短语可看作是“半施动者”。关于 at 的这种用法将在 9.63 和 16.69 中进一步举例说明。

“刺激因素”的概念有时由其他介词表示。这些介词代替 at，具有半施动者的功能(参见3.76):

I'm worried about this. ["This worries me."]
He's interested in history. ["History interests him."]
His plans were known to everyone. ["Everyone knew his plans."]

【注】

在英国英语中，当刺激因素是人或物而不是事件时，用 with 而不用 at:

I was furious with John.
I was delighted with the present.

但在美国英语中，用 at 颇为常见：

I was furious/angry/livid/mad at Christine.
如果刺激因素是抽象名词，at 不论在英国英语还是美国英语里都是成立的：
I was furious at Christine's behaviour.
at 常被 about 代替：annoyed at/about, pleased at/about 等。
(参见 16.69 中更多的例子)

##### 伴随：with

I'm so glad you're coming with us. [1] Jack, (together) with several of his noisy friends, was drinking till after 2 in the morning. [2] 在例[2]中，with.短语所起的作用非常接近于用and的并列形式。但须注意with与and不同，with和单数动词连用（参见13.103）：Jack and several of his noisy friends were... [2a]下面是伴随短语作后置修饰语的一个例子：Curry with rice is my favourite dish. 在这一意义上，和其他大多数意义一样（参见9.53），without是with的反义词（等于“unaccompanied by”）：You never see him without his dog. She was without her children. Without you, I'm not going. with还用来表示“伴随情况”，如例[3]；或引进一个主语（参见9.55，14.15ff），如例[4]：With all the noise, she was finding it hard to concentrate.

It all started with John('s) being late for dinner. [4] 在这两种用法中，with 暗示了原因的含义：例 [3] 隐含了“because of all the noise...”的意思：例 [4] 则隐含了“It all started as a result of John('s) being late...”的意思。

支持和反对：for，with，against

9.53 for 表示支持的含义 ["in favour of"); with 表示团结一致或同情的含义:

Are you for or against the plan? ["Do you support or oppose the plan?"]
Remember that every one of us is with you. ["on your side"]

在这种用法中，与 with 相对立的否定词不是 without，而是 against:

It is prudent to go with rather than against the tide of public opinion.
the movement against nuclear arms ["anti-nuclear"; 参见态度前缀，附录 I.25]

然而，with 表示了人与人之间对抗的含义，如 fight with，quarrel with，argue with 等。试比较：

动词 fight 与介词 with 连用，在 fight with somebody 中表示“对抗”的含义。这个短语的意思可以是“fight somebody”（参见9.31）或“fight against somebody”；然而，with 在 fight with X against Y 中表示“支持”的含义[“on X's side”]。但是 fight 在如下短语中不用介词，如 fight a bad cause, fight an illness，下面例句中的 play、可采用两种结构：

I played (a game of) chess with Sam.
Sam at chess.

介词的其他含义

##### of 表示的各种关系

9.54 of 是最常用的介词，主要用作名词短语中的后置修饰语，它的功能与属格相似(参见 5.115ff)，如：

the gravity of the earth~the earth's gravity

属格与 of-结构的对应关系放在名词短语一章内讨论最为方便（参见17.38ff）。

然而，作后置修饰的 of-短语还有范围很广的其他用法（参见5.6ff），如：

(a) part of the city [部分]
a kind of wood [品种]
a lot of people [数量]

以下是使用 of-短语的其他例子：

the courage of the man ["the courage that the man shows"]

a typewriter of my father's ["a typewriter that my father has"]

the envy of the world ["the envy that the world feels"]

the trial of the conspirators ["the trial that the conspirators face"]

the virtue of thrift ["the virtue that consists in thrift"]

a flock of sheep ["a flock that is made up of sheep"]

a glass of water ["a glass that contains water"]

seven of my friends ["seven from among my friends"]

people of the Middle Ages ["people who lived in the Middle Ages"]

the house of my dreams ["the house which I see in my dreams"]

the College of Surgeons ["the college to which surgeons belong"]

a boat of fibreglass ["a boat made of fibreglass"]

##### “有”: of, with, without

9.55 例 [1] 中的含义贯穿于例 [1a—1d] 所有的名词短语之中：

The man has courage. [1]

the man having courage. [1a]

the man's courage [1b]
the courage of the man [1c]
a man of courage [1d]

例[1c]和[1d]都有作后置修饰语的of-短语。它们之间的区别在于例[1c]的中心词(the courage)是意念上的宾语(notional object)，而例[1d]的中心词(the man)是意念上的主语。在例[1d]这种结构中，of仅限于表示抽象的属性，如：

a pianist of great talent ["a very talented pianist"]
a performance of distinction ["a distinguished performance"]
“有”的概念更经常由 with 来表达，尤其与具体特征连用时：
a man with a red nose ["who has a red nose"; "a red-nosed man"]
an industrialist with a house on the Costa Brava ["who has a house...]
a woman with a large family
a box with a carved lid

试比较下列结构，例[2]既能用 of 又能用 with，但在例[3]中只有with才是通常情况下可以成立的形式：

a woman  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}of \\ with\end{array}\right\} $ strong feelings[抽象][2]
a woman  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}of \\ with\end{array}\right\} $ strong hands[具体][3]

with 的反义词是 without（参见 9.52）：

a play without any faults ["a play with no faults"]
women without children ["childless women"]
the house without a porch ["...which has no porch"]
含有 with 或 without 的短语与含有 have 的关系分句之间的对应关系也适用于 have-存在句(参见 18.54):
the girl who has a boyfriend in the navy
~the girl with a boyfriend in the navy
with 和 without 还能引导在名词短语中作后置修饰语的 非限定性分句或无动词分句：
the factory with its smoking chimney
a room with its door open

此外，它们还能引导作状语用的限定性和无动词分句：

He wandered in without shoes or socks on.
With so many essays to write, I won't have time to go out tonight.

与之对应的较完全的分句是分词状语分句，表示意外情况（contingency）（参见15.46）：

Having so many essays to write, I won't have time to go out tonight.

由于起这些功能的 with 和 without 引导分句，因而它们是从属连词，不是介词。非限定性分句也可以是一个 to-不定式。试比较：

With Mary being away
With no one to talk to
With Mary away
With the house empty
Without anyone to talk to

John felt miserable.

在这种结构中，with 和 without 的后面要求接名词短语（不一定作主语）：

 $ ^{*} $With being away...

这又一次表明，它们在这里起的功能不是介词，而是从属连词（参见14.15）。介词可以带-ing分句，但不能带作补足语用的to-不定式分句（参见9.2）：

*On arriving* Mary took a taxi.

with 和 without 引导的分句的功能类似于下面例句中 for 的功能(参见14.6):

I bought a car for Mary to drive to work in.

同时，我们必须认清它们的连接词用法和介词用法之间的关系。试比较：

With Mary I always feel happy.
Without Mary I always feel miserable.
I bought a car for Mary (so that she could drive to work in it).

【注】

在这一组中，without 有两个含义：(a) “not with”(没有得到……)

以及(b)“outside”(在……的外边):

(a) They work both with and without assistance from me.

(b) They operate both \{within and without\} the organization.

然而，要注意其中存在不平衡，即第二种含义的 without 只能用于它与 within 并列的时候：

(a) They work {with}assistance from me.
(b) They operate {within} the organization.

让步：in spite of, despite, for all, with all 等

9.56 in spite of 是常用的让步介词，despite 是较为正式的用词：

I admire him, in spite of his faults.
Despite strong pressure from the government, the unions have refused to order a return to work.
with all 和 for all ("despite")更加口语化，它们的用法极其有限：
With all his boasting and ostentatious training, he was knocked out in the first round.
在让步用法中，两个介词都必须与 all 连用：with all 和 for all，在表示原因时，all 可有可无：with 或 with all。试比较：

With all this noise I managed to get some sleep. [让步]
For all
"in spite of"]
With all this noise,I couldn't sleep. [原因：“because of”]

notwithstanding ["in spite of"] 用于正式文体，颇有法律文体的性质，尤其用于后置时：

Thomas Carlyle, {notwithstanding his tedious rhetoric,} {his tedious rhetoric notwithstanding,}
is a master of the sublime in prose style.

试比较 notwithstanding 的状语用法，如：
Notwithstanding, the case must be prosecuted. ["not withstanding any conditions"]

##### 方面：with reference to, with regard to, as for 等

9.57 有些表示方面的介词用于相当正式的语境，尤其用于商业信函中：

With reference to [不太常用: In reference to] your letter/request/enquiry of April 29th, I confirm my Directors' agreement to advance a further sum of £2000.〈正式用法〉

With regard to the date of delivery... [不太常用：In regard to 或 Re/ri://; 这种介词常在此类信中引进二等或末等话题]

re 具有类似 with regard to 的功能，但是 Re 用于短笺比用于正式信函更为常见，如：

Re your idea of extending the canteen...

属于这同一含义范围的其他介词还有：regarding，with respect to，in respect of，respecting，on the matter of，about，concerning，as to(参见话题,9.60)。

as to 的功能类似 with regard to, as regards 等:

As to the question you raise in your last letter, I think that...

as to 还用于表示“according to”的含义，如 correct as to size and colour.

另一方面，as for 引导话题的转换，所以它通常不能用在一篇话语的开始。它有“转到……话题上”的含义，在文体上不如其他表示方面的复杂介词那样正式：

We had a delightful weekend in the country. As for the traffic, we had no difficulty.

as for 用在句首常常表示“轻蔑的态度”：

As for his book, I suppose you've read the reviews! 有许多属于本范围、而与动词有同源关系的边缘介词 (marginal

prepositions): concerning, regarding 和 touching〈正式用法〉(参见 9.8), 如：

Concerning the recent proposal by the chairperson, I suggest we...

considering 的用法类似 in view of ["taking into consideration"], 常常表示“if one takes into account the rather surprising fact that”（假如考虑到颇为惊人的事实……）的含义：

Considering the job situation, there were surprisingly few applications this year.

作状语表示方面的介词短语主要用作外加状语或联加状语。它们之中大多数还能在名词短语中作后置修饰语：

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://pplines-online.bj.bcebos.com/deploy/official/paddleocr/pp-ocr-vl-16-online//b56e7978-a6b8-4654-acbd-3cc2247cb362/markdown_0/imgs/img_in_image_box_151_395_658_467.jpg?authorization=bce-auth-v1%2FALTAKDN8mY5KlNI7zaRpLmOqrw%2F2026-11-03T02%3A20%3A46Z%2F-1%2F%2Fc98ea797ec61b5fdcaabc8b33a4164170f4418294261d5e9202fb3dbf28e6c70" alt="Image" width="67%" /></div>


We await your decision as to whether these repairs are to be carried out immediately.

【注】

以 irregardless (of)代替 regardless (of) 的用法相当流行，尤其在美国英语中，但是多数人认为这是非标准的用法。这似乎是由于将 regardless 和 irrespective 混淆起来，或者是由于选用了被人们认为是为强调适当的双重否定(ir+less)造成的。

##### 例外和附加

9.58 表示例外的最常用的介词是：except for，with the exception of，apart from，aside from〈尤其是美国英语〉，except, excepting, excluding，but 和 save〈正式用法〉。表示例外的介词主要在状语中有外加状语的功能(参见8.121ff):

We had a pleasant time, except for the weather.
With the exception of James, none of us had any
money.

The worst period of my life, $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}apart from the war,\\aside from the war\\<尤其美国英语>\end{array}\right\} $ was

when I was out of work.

except 和 excepting 通常用于后置修饰语中，but 却只能用于后置修饰语中：

All {but {except(ing)}}the captain were rescued.
Finally we had packed everything {but {except}} the type-writer.
Any time but now. ["any other time"]

所以，but 不能作为介词出现在句首：

 $ ^{*} $But
Except for}me, everyone was tired.

在这类结构中，介词短语经常与它的名词中心词隔开，并后移到分句的末尾（参见18.39非连续名词短语）：

Everyone but me was tired.~Everyone was tired but me.

此外，带 but-修饰语的名词短语必须包括一个限定词和一个表示确切意义（肯定或否定）的不定代词：no, all, any, every, each, nobody, anywhere, everything 等或一个 wh-疑问词（who? where? 等）。所以，我们可以说 all but one，但不能说*some but one，

也不能说*many but one. 其他例子还有：

This car is anything but slow.
We've bought everything but milk.
Who should turn up but our old friend Tom.
bar 和 barring 代替 except 和 excepting 的情况较为罕见：
This is the most versatile microcomputer on the market, bar none.
Barring accidents, we'll be there on time.
beyond 有时用于非断定语境，表示 except (for) 的含义：
Beyond the press release, there are no further comments.
He didn't help, beyond showing a mild interest.
附加含义可以由 beside, as well as 和 in addition to 来表示，例如：

There were three people present { besides { in addition to } the

committee.
As well as learning to swim he has been taking Spanish lessons this summer.

试比较下面的例句中 except，but（两者都表示例外含义）与 besides（表示附加含义）之间的词义差别：

Everyone passed  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} except \\ but \end{array}\right\} $ Richard. ["Richard did not pass but everyone else did."]
Everyone passed besides Richard.["Everyone passed, in addition to Richard."]
在否定句中，这种差别就消失了，所以下面两句是同义的：
No one passed  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} except \\ besides \end{array}\right\} $ Richard.

##### 【注】

[a] 必须将作介词用的 but 与作连接词用的 but (参见 13.5ff) 区别开来。两种功能的相似和不同之处可以从下面两句中看出：

Everyone had a good time but John. [介词=“with the exception of”, “except for”]

The students had a good time. {but not John.} {but John did not.} [连接词]

然而，except 和 but 究竟是介词还是连接词常常很难断定，这可以从下面例句结构的可变性中看出来：

He does everything in the house {except} {but} {putting} the children to bed.

[b] 我们从上面看到，例外介词和附加介词常常用介词短语或分句作它们的补足语(参见9.1【注】[d]):
except in the southeast
apart from when I last spoke to you
except for what I ordered
in addition to being a fine colleague

[c] all but 的组合在口语中作强化语：
He all but ["very nearly"] strangled me.

试比较：She is but ["only"] a child.(其中 but 是限制性下加状语，参见 8.116【注】【b】)

##### 否定的条件: but for

9.59 but for 不是用来表示例外，而是表示“某种否定的条件”：

But for Gordon, we would have lost the match. ["If it hadn't been for Gordon", "If Gordon hadn't played as he did...," 等]

许多人将 except for 和 but for 一样用于表示否定的条件。然而，except for 通常表示例外(参见9.58)。注意以下两句的不同含义：

Except for John they {would all have died. ["If it hadn't been for John ..."]

all died. ["With the exception of John..."]

#### 主要用作动词和形容词补足成分的介词短语

##### 话题: about, on

9.60 about 和 on 作“关于……的问题”，“有关……”解时，可以和相当多的动词和形容词（参见 16.28, 16.69）搭配，例如：

She is lecturing  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} \text{about} \\ \text{on} \end{array}\right\} $ new techniques of management.

He told me {about}his adventures.

##### 其他例子有：

ABOUT/ON

argue about/on

ABOUT

be knowledgeable about/on

communicate about/on

find out about

confer about/on

hold forth about/on

hear about

preach about/on

speak about/on

inform (someone) about

write about/on

learn about

keep quiet about

quarrel about

read about

teach(someone)about

on 主要用于有准备的正式语言交流（演说、讲课、写作等）之中，因此在 chat 或 quarrel 一类动词之后用 on 不合适。所以例 [1] 会使人感到她在发表正式演说[“gave a lecture on”]，而例 [2] 则很可能是非正式的谈话或是指偶然谈到：

She spoke on butterflies. about butterflies.

后置修饰短语（其中 on 和 about 表示 “on the subject of” （关于……的问题））也会出现这种含义上的差别：

a book about/on butterflies a story about a princess
a talk about/on antiques ignorance about sex
a discussion about/on the facts about nuclear drugs power
a word about/on the garden a fuss about nothing

由 about 和 on 引导的介词短语与动词 be 一起作不可省略的调体附加状语：

This book is  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l}on \\ about\end{array}\right\} $ stamps.

concerning(参见9.57)可以替代 about 和 on,但比较少见,多半用于正式语体中,如 a dispute concerning land rights.

over 也用来表示 “on the subject of”，“in connection with”：

They quarrelled over money.
It's no use crying over spilt milk.

在 tell, speak, talk, inform...of 等结构中，of 可以代替 about，但比较少见，多见于书面语中，about 和 of 常常与 think 连用，但含义不同：

He thought  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} \text { about the problem. } \left[\text { "He pondered/considered the problem." } \right] \\ \text { of the problem. }\left[\text { "He brought the problem to his mind." } \right] \end{array}\right. $

of 在名词短语中也可以代替 about（参见上面的例子），例如：

a story of a princess ignorance of sex the facts of nuclear power

材料、成分：with, of, out of; 物质：from

9.61 with 与“制作”动词(verbs of “making”)连用，表示一种成分；而 of 和 out of 则指整个东西的材料或成分；from 表示作为某物来源的一种物质：

This cake is made with lots of eggs. ["Eggs are an important ingredient.]
He made the frame (out) of wood. ["Wood was the only material."]
Beer is made from hops.

with 还用于遍布性词组，如 paved with brick, filled with water, loaded with hay(参见 9.29)。

of 与表示“物质”的名词连用，作后置修饰语和状语：

a bracelet of solid gold ["made out of", "a solid gold bracelet"]
a table of polished oak ["made/consisting of polished oak", "a polished oak table"]

of 还可以用在比喻中：

a man of steel
a heart of stone [参见“a woman of/with strong feelings”, 9.55]

标准: for, at

9.62 比较形容词必须（不论是明确地还是含蓄地）与比较基础（参见7.86）相关联。所以，如果没有这种隐含的比较关系；我们就不能用[1]：
This boy is bigger.
[1]
同样地，没有比较形式的等级形容词隐含某种标准或规格的意思；例[2]与例[3]中的big含意是不同的：
This elephant is big.
[2]
This cat is big.
[3]

这是因为“象之大”的标准与规格自然要比“猫之大”的标准与规格高大得多。

我们可以用一个“for”短语(例[4—5])表明这个标准：

He's not bad for a youngster. ["considering that he is a youngster"]
That dog is long-legged for a terrier.

确定等级形容词或名词的含义，还有一个办法：用 at 表示方面（其中的形容词适合于主语）（参见 16.69），如例 [6—7]：

He's good/clever/brilliant/an expert at organizing things.
He's bad/better/terrible/no good at games.

for 和 at 的这种用法并不限于形容词补足成分，如以下例子所示，这些介词还有其他不少语法功能：

I'm a complete dunce at mathematics.
She's getting on very well at her job.
For an Englishman, he speaks foreign languages remarkably well.
It's a dreadfully expensive toy for what it is.

反应：at, to

### 9.63 现在探讨以下三个句子：

Their rejection of the offer surprised me. [1]
I was surprised by their rejection of the offer. [1a]
I was surprised at their rejection of the offer. [1b]

例[1]通过直截了当的主语一动词一宾语结构，显示出一件事情、一种情感反应以及产生这种反应的人之间的关系。这种关系同样可以用被动语态[1a]（参见3.63ff）表示，或者也可在被动语态的句子中用at代替施动词by[1b]。这里的at（像我们在9.51中见到的那样）表示情感反应及其刺激因素之间的关系。这一语境中的surprised是分词形容词（注意它前面可以加very；参见7.15），at（表示“刺激因素”）正是专门和这一类形容词形成搭配的（参见3.76，16.69）：

alarmed at disgusted at amused at delighted at

动词和非分词形容词也有这类结构，但比较少见：

laugh/stare/gaze/glance/aim/rejoice...at be angry/glad...at

另一种表达相同意思的方法是让主句表示充当“刺激因素”的事

情，而让反应由介词+表示情感的抽象名词来表达，例如：to my regret, to my annoyance, to my relief, to my surprise, to my horror, to my delight:

To my regret, they rejected the offer.

to my regret 在本语境中是内容外加状语，类似副词 regrettable (参见 8.127)。

人的反应也可以由 to + 人称代词或由 to + 物主代词 + mind, in + 物主代词 + opinion 等组成的短语表示出来：

To me,
To my mind, their rejection was a surprise.
In my opinion,

在这一意义上，to 并不限于感情的反应，它同样适用于理智和感觉的反应：

To a mind based in common sense, his ideas are utterly absurd.
It looked to me like a vast chasm.

然而，在上面最后一例中，to-短语不是外加状语，而是附加状语。

according to 与其说它表示对事情的反应，还不如说它是对事情作出的解释。它主要用于第三人称(参见 8.127【注】[a])：

To him/you/me
According to him/you/??me} this is quite unexpected.

【注】

according to 这种用法应与含义不同的 in accordance/agreement/conformity with 区分开来：

in accordance with according to the new regulations

#### 对介词短语的修饰

9.64 介词的含义(尤其是时间和地点介词)可用表示程度和范围的修饰语。因此介词（像很多形容词和副词那样）之前可以用强化语(参见7.61)。例如：

I left it just <inside> the garage. ["a little way"].

He had wandered right off the path. ["completely"]

Now their footsteps could be heard directly <above>my head.

I got up just/soon <after> ten.

There was rubbish all〈over〉the place.

They followed close <behind> me.

This cake mix comes straight <out of> the packet.

The dog was lying right  $ \langle $in the middle of\rangle $ the floor. 在以上例子中，强化语究竟是修饰整个介词短语，还是只修饰介词，是存在着疑义的。然而，在上述例子中强化语可以修饰介词副词，例如：right in the middle 等。

#### 介词和介词副词

9.65 介词副词是一个小品词，它在形式上与介词相同或与介词相关联，在功能上常常像省略了补足语的介词：

 $$ \begin{aligned}&A\text{car drove}\begin{cases}past\ the\ door.&[past\ 是介词]\\past.&[past\ 是介词副词]\end{cases}\end{aligned} $$ 

所以，介词副词的形式与介词相同，但句法功能不同。它可以单独出现，用作附加状语、联加状语、后置修饰语等，无需加上介词补语：

Despite the fine weather, we stayed in all day. Besides, I don't feel like a walk just now. The day before, I had spoken to her in the office.

介词副词通常重读，而简单介词(尤其是单音节介词，参见9.9)则通常不重读。在以下三对例句中，每对第一句的in是重读的副词，而第二句的in则是非重读的介词：

{She stayed IN. [1]
She stayed in the HOUSE. [1a]
He thrust IN his HAND. [2]
He swam in the LAKE. [2a]
Which prisoner did they march IN? [3]
Which uniform did they MARCH in? [3a]

介词和副词通常和它们前面的动词一起构成习惯语的组合，例如：

make for, make up, make up for.然而，这里我们将只注意它们作为单个词项的含义和句法功能，至于习惯用法，则与其说是语法所关心的问题，不如说是词典所关心的问题。关于短语动词与介词动词（即在句法或语义上作为单一的单位看待的动词+副词/动词+介词的组合）将在16.2ff中讨论。

【注】

介词副词与介词短语例 [4] 之间的关系可以比作某些动词的及物与不及物用法[5](参见 16.19) 之间的关系：

She stayed in (the house).
She ate (breakfast).

9.66 (a) 下表包括与简单介词(参见 9.7) 相关联的一些介词副词，例如：

Why didn't you come before 7 o'clock?
a'board a'bout a'bove
a'cross after a'long
a'longside a'round be'fore
be'hind be'low be'neath
be'sides be'tween be'yond
by down in
in'side near ('nearer, 'nearest) off
on 'opposite out'side
over past round
since through through'out
under under'neath up
with'in with'out

除了 without 和联加状语 besides 以外，所有介词副词基本上都是时间或空间附加状语

(b) 下表包括与复杂(两个词的)宾语(参见9.10)相关联的一些介词副词，例如：

Paul wants to go to the Zoo {instead of going to a museum.
instead.

a'head a'way back
close east 等 'eastward(s) 等
in'stead out over'head
to'gether

(c) 下表包括与复杂(三个词的)介词（参见 9.11）相关联的一些介词副词，例如：

Why don't you put the trunk on top of the car?
at variance in addition in aid
in case in charge in common
in comparison in context in exchange
in favour in front in lieu
in line in need in relation
in return on top

9.7ff中列出的大多数普通介词也能作介词副词，例如：

位置(9.16): Is your sister in?
No, she's out/away.

目的地(9.16): She went out/away/in.

通过(9.24): The dog jumped over/through.

路线(9.26): Move along.
She came round to see me.

方位(9.27): The man (who sat) opposite kept looking at her.

结果(9.28): The price of oil is up again today.

遍及(9.29): There were lots of people around.

介词短语和介词副词可以看作是位于标尺的两个极端，明晰度从例[1]依次到例[5]逐步降低。在“They are all...”句型中，我们可以有以下几种形式：

(in great) favour of the proposal [1]
(greatly) in favour of the proposal [2]
(greatly) in favour of it [3]
(greatly) in its favour [4]
(greatly) in favour [5]

在例[1]中，我们有以 favour（它前面可加形容词修饰语）为中心词的

自由句 $ ^{①} $名词短语(free syntatic noun phrase)；在例[2]中有一个以the proposal为补足语的复杂介词in favour of：在例[3]中代词替换了例[2]中的名词性补足语；在例[4]中，用了所有格限定词its；在例[5]中用的是介词副词in favour，其词义依赖于前面语境或实境中提及的情况。与例[2]和例[3](用后置修饰语)相比，例[4]的紧缩处理(用前置修饰语)与名词短语相关。从例[4]到例[5]的一步是超越前置修饰语结构的一步。

##### 【注】

[a] for 和 against 用作介词副词只出现于 votes for and against 一类的短语中。

[b] to 在 set 'to (and finish), turn 'to (and help) 和 (walk) to and fro 之类的短语中用作介词副词。试比较在 walk to and from work 中的介词短语。

[c] 不存在与 contrary to (参见 9.10) 相对应的介词副词。但要注意缩略词组 to the contrary 的类似用法。

His vote was {contrary to mine. to the contrary.}

再比较联加状语(8.137)用法：

On the contrary, what I said was this year,

To the contrary,〈美国英语〉 not next.

#### 分句句型

##### 简单句和多重句

10.1 句子不外乎简单(SIMPLE)句和多重(MULTIPLE)句两类。简单句由单一的独立分句构成。多重句包含一个或者多个分句作为直接成分。多重句可以是联合句(COMPOUND)，也可以是复合句(COMPLEX)。联合句的直接构成成分是两个或两个以上并列分句(COORDINATE clauses)。复合句用从属分句(SUBORDINATE clause)来担任句中一个或一个以上成分，例如直接宾语或状语。（详见14.1ff）。

像主语和动词这样的成分既是构成句子的成分，又是句子中构成分句的成分。以后每当我们的论述既适用于句子又适用于构成句子的分句时，就一概使用分句和分句结构这两个名称。因此对含有一个从属分句的复合句可以按两个层次来分析，一个层次是分析整个句子，另一个层次是分析包括在句子中的从属分句：

<div style="text-align: center;"><img src="https://pplines-online.bj.bcebos.com/deploy/official/paddleocr/pp-ocr-vl-16-online//90834cb7-950f-4cfc-b50e-3a95f6e47407/markdown_1/imgs/img_in_chart_box_174_613_608_904.jpg?authorization=bce-auth-v1%2FALTAKDN8mY5KlNI7zaRpLmOqrw%2F2026-11-03T02%3A21%3A00Z%2F-1%2F%2F5f63b893eaf577928b195d93e1b72afe60b0c18078c9d6777db16ebc3ef1642f" alt="Image" width="57%" /></div>


<div style="text-align: center;"><div style="text-align: center;">图 10.1 句子和分句成分</div> </div>


在本章中，我们主要讨论的是简单句。对并列分句的讨论要推后

到第13章，对从属分句的讨论则要推后到第14章和15章而且本章所论述的内容只限于简单句所包含的主要成分：主语、动词、宾语和补语几个方面。和其他的分句成分相比，状语这个成分一般说来更具有可分离性，也更灵活，因此在第8章中对它作了详细论述。

##### 【注】

[a] 我们使用“简单句”这一术语，指的是一个独立分句，这个独立分句不包含另一个作为其成分的分句。因此，例[1]是个复合句，句中的 if you need it 起状语作用：

You can borrow my car if you need it. [1]

但是，简单句也可以包含一个在短语中起作用的分句。在这种情况下，复合性表现在短语这一层次，而不是表现在句子或分句的层次。因此例[2]是个简单句：

You can borrow the car that belongs to my sister. [2] 在例[2]中，关系分句 that belongs to my sister 是 the car that belongs to my sister 这个作宾语的复合名词短语里的后置修饰语。修饰名词短语的分句将在第17章中讨论。作形容词短语补足语的分句将在第16章中加以讨论。

和本书不同，“简单句”这一术语在其他语法书中经常用来指一个不包含另一分句的独立分句，而不管所包含的分句是不是句子的直接成分。有些语法书，把非限定结构（这种结构含有一个非限定动词作为动词成分）看作是短语而不是分句。我们则把这种结构看作是分句，因为可以把它分解为分句成分（参见14.5）。非限定分句本身就是从属性质的，因此不能成为典型的简单句形式（另见11.41）。

在不是内行的人看来，简单句并不一定简单。例如，由于其中的短语复杂，一个简单句可能是很复杂的：

On the recommendation of the committee, the temporary chairman, who had previous experience of the medical issues concerned, made the decision that no further experiments on living animals should be conducted in circumstances that might lead to unfavourable press publicity.

除了短语的复杂性这一点之外，其他一些因素将在14.2中谈到。

##### 分句结构

10.2 现在我们回过来进一步论述在 2.13ff 里简略谈过的分句结构。在那一章节中，我们把分句成分按功能分成五种类型。对其中的三种类型又作了进一步的划分。

主语 (S)

动词 (V)

宾语 (O)——直接宾语 $ (O_{d}) $

——间接宾语 $ O_{1} $

补语 (C)——主语补语 $ (C_{s}) $

——宾语补语 $ (C_{0}) $

状语 (A)——与主语相关的状语(A.)——与宾语相关的状语(A。)

通过去掉随意状语，根据七类功能在允许范围内可能的各种组合，我们归纳出七种主要分句类型。下页表10.2以句子的典型形式——简单陈述句为例来说明正常词序的主要分句类型。

分句的类型取决于动词成分中的全义动词属于哪一类动词，不同类别的动词需要不同的补语(O_{d}, O_{i}, C_{s}, C_{c}, A)来补足动词的意义，或者不需要补语(在SV类型中，动词是不及物的)。

##### 动词的多重归类

10.3 必须记住，一个特定的动词，由于它有着多种不同的含义，可以分别属于几个不同的类别（参见附录 I.54），因而可以用在几个不同的分句类型中。动词 get 是个特别活跃的动词，只有 SV 型不能用它（即使是 SV 型，也不是绝对不能用 get，参见【注】）：

SVO He'll get a surprise.
SVC He's getting angry.
SVA He got through the window.
SVOO He got her a splendid present.
SVOC He got his shoes and socks wet.
SVOA He got himself into trouble.
