<div style="text-align: center;"><div style="text-align: center;">图 15.35 假设条件句中谓语动词的形式</div> </div>


关于谓语动词的形式，详见 14.23。

条件分句——具体说来是由 if，in case 和 in the event that 引导的分句——与问句相像之处是，一般说来对回答的期待是没有倾

向性的或倾向于否定的回答(参见11.6f)。因此，条件分句像疑问句一样，往往容纳非断定形式(参见10.60f)：

In the event that he is at all interested, I'll speak to him.

If you ever touch me again, I'll scream.
If you had ever listened to any of my lectures, you would have known the answer.
She's taking a stick with her in case she has any trouble on the way.

非断定词项也出现在间接条件中（参见 15.38）：

They're going steady, if it's of any interest to you. ["I don't know if it's of any interest to you."]
I'll be in my office all DAY, in case you have any PRÓBlem at all. ["I'm telling you this in case you have any problem at all."]

大多数从属连词不出现或很少出现在假设条件中。它们引导的分句中往往用断定形式：

I won't phone you, unless something unforeseen happens. 再提的 if-分句中可以用断定形式：

A: I've got something to tell you later.
B: Well, if you've got something to tell me, tell me now.

##### 【注】

[a] 开放条件句也称为“真实”(real)“事实”(factual)和“中性”(neutral)条件句。假设条件句也称为“封闭”(closed)、“非真实”(unreal)、“否决”(rejected)、“非事实”(nonfactual)、“反事实”(counterfactual)和“有标记”(marked)条件句。

[b] if 和 when 有时用于将来开放条件句。

[c] if only 是 if 的强化形式，主要用于假设条件分句，表示讲话人所祈愿的事情会发生、正在发生或早该发生：

If only you would help me next week, I would not be so nervous.

If only they were here now, we would be able to

celebrate their wedding anniversary.

If only somebody had told us, we could have warned you.

如果是肯定的，条件分句中一般用断定形式，而且几乎总是放在母句之前。条件分句有时单独使用，表示一种假设的祈愿（参见11.41）：If only I hadn't lost it! only if 组合，则情形完全不同：if 受指心词 only 限制。

[d] given (that) 和 assuming (that) 用来表示讲话人认为曾经，已经或将会实现的，并由此可得出一种断言的开放条件。一个由 granted (that) 引导的分句也可用作供推理用的前提条件，但通常暗示前面有一个该前提赖以成立的陈述。if 也可以这样使用：If you were there (and you say you were), you must have seen her；带分句代用式的 if-分句(如 if so, if not, if that's true, if that's the case 和 (带非断定词的) if anything, if at all)也可这样使用。given (that) 和 granted(that) 往往用于正式的书面语体，尤其用于论证。

[e] as long as 和 so long as 在语义上与 provided (that) 和 providing (that) 相似，但不如它们正式。just so (that) 往往出现在非正式的会话中。它们的意思是 “if and only if”。

[f] unless 引导一个否定条件；unless-分句通常大致与一个否定的 if-分句相近。用 unless 就更加强调例外条件（“only if... not”）。因此，在有些语境中不能使用 unless-分句：

I'll feel much happier{if he doesn't come with us.

*Unless you had studied hard,

}you'd have failed the exam.

[g] in case (参见 15.46)用于开放条件句，一般指将来时间 ("if it should happen that"):

I'll let you know in case they come by here.

在正式的美国英语中，in case 也有 “on condition that” 的

在正式的美国英语中，in case 也有 “on condition that” 的。意思：

The verb is plural (only/just) in case the subject is

plural.

[h] 在开放条件句中，in the event (that)一般可以取代 if. 因其较长，所以显得臃肿。

[i] if and only if 这个形式用于数学和形式逻辑，为母句的真实性引导一个必要而又充分的条件。这个形式有时缩简为 iff.

##### 条件分句中的动词短语

15.36 条件分句中，有时不用一般现在时态而用现在时虚拟式语气来表示开放条件：

If any vehicle be found parked on these premises without written permission, it shall be towed away at the expense of the vehicle's owner.

这种用法主要限于十分正式的、法律的或准法律的语境中。

表示假设条件句的两种方法偶尔用于正式的语境中。它们带有试探性的含义：

(i) was to 或 were to + 不定式:

If it  $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} was \\ were \end{array}\right\} $ to rain, the ropes would snap. They're far too tight. [1]

(ii) should+不定式(参见 14.25 推定 should):

If a serious crisis should arise, the public would have to be informed of its full implications.

例[1]中的 were 是 be 的单数过去时虚拟语气形式而不是一般过去时的形式，因为在过去时虚拟语气中 were 不仅用于复数，而且用于单数(参见 3.62)。如例[1]所示，无论过去时虚拟语气形式还是过去时陈述语气形式，都可用来表示假设条件，许多人，尤其在正式的书面英语中，爱用虚拟语气。

If John $ \left\{\begin{array}{l} was \\ were \end{array}\right\} $here, we would soon learn the truth.

习语 if I...you 习惯上通常用虚拟语气的 were，虽然 was 也常有所见。

我们可以不用从属连词而用主语-功能词倒装来标明条件关系。在条件分句中，这种倒装形式用得最多的是功能词 had:

Had I known, I would have written before. ["If I had known,..."]

当分句是否定句时，not 置于实义动词之前，不可用前接成分：

Had I not seen it with my own eyes, I would not have believed it.

在多少带有一点文学色彩的语体中，虚拟语气的 were 和试探性的 should 也可用倒装形式：

Were it to reveal its secrets, that house would collapse in shame.
Were she in charge, she would do things differently. Should you change your mind, no one would blame you.
Should she be interested, I'll phone her.

功能词 could 和 might 用倒装就更罕见了：

Might Could I but see my native land, I would die a happy man.

这两个功能词用这种倒装结构在实义动词前就需要一个如 but 或 just 之类的副词。

关于在条件分句和母句中动词的选用，参见 14.23。

##### 修辞性条件分句

15.37 修辞性条件分句似乎是表示一个开放条件，但是（像修辞性问句一样，参见11.23）它们实际上是作一种有力的陈述。修辞性if-分句有两类：一类是陈述出自该条件分句，另一类是陈述出自母句。

(a) 如果母句中的陈述显然是荒谬的，那末条件分句中的陈述就是不真实的：

If they're Irish, I'm the Pope. ["Since I'm obviously not the Pope, they're certainly not Irish."]

If you believe that, you'll believe anything. ["You certainly can't believe that."]

If she doesn't get first prize, she's no daughter of yours. ["She certainly will get first prize."]

就是真实的。这类条件分句和度量词语连用时，暗示至少有条件分句中所述的度量。这种 if-分句放在句末：

He's ninety if he's a day. ["If you'll agree that he's at least a day old, perhaps you'll take my word that he's ninety."]
The package weighed ten pounds if it weighed an ounce. ["The package certainly weighed ten pounds."]
The painting must be worth a thousand dollars if it's worth a cent. ["The painting must certainly be worth a thousand dollars."]

【注】

(a) 类中的母句有一些显然表示不真实的固定说法，只是主语有些变动而已，如 I'll eat my hat 和 He's a Dutchman:

If Dave's younger than me, I'll eat my hat. ["Dave's certainly not younger than me."]

I'll be (或 I'm) damned 和 I'll be (或 I'm) hanged 是更为固定的说法；因为主语只能用 I。两者的语体都很随便：

[ˈɪl beɪˈdæmnedɪf I apologize. [ˈɪl certainly not apologize.]]

因此，这些固定的说法都可以单独用来表示惊奇，例如：Well，I'll be damned. 在带修辞性条件分句的母句里也有用禁忌语的（如：Fuck me if I'm going to lift a finger to help them）.

还请与 She's nothing if not tough ["She's certainly tough."] 和 He's nothing if not cruel ["He's certainly cruel."] 中的固定句型比较。

##### 间接条件

15.38 间接条件都是取决于话语的含蓄言语行为(参见11.3)的开放条件(参见15.35)，因此是语体外加状语(参见15.21)。间接条件主要由if-分句充当。语体外加状语可分为如下几类：

(a) 条件分句是一个礼貌习惯用语，使讲话人的话语似乎有赖于听话人的许可(参见 8.124f):

If you don't mind my saying so, your slip is showing [“If you don't mind my saying so, I'm telling you that...”]

If I may be quite frank with you, I don't approve of any concessions to ignorance.

其他例子有：

if I may say so (without contradiction), if I may put it bluntly, if I may be personal, if you can be serious for just this once, if you can keep a secret, if we can be practical for a moment, if I may put the matter as simply as possible, if I may interrupt, if I may change the subject

(b) 条件分句是一种缓和话语措辞的元语言评述（参见 8.126），或暗示用语并不十分精确，或暗示不要误解讲话人的本意。它若明若暗地要求听话人赞同：

His style is florid, if that's the right word. ["I'm not sure that florid is the right word."] [1]
The Big Bang Theory of the origin of the universe bears a startling resemblance to the description of creation in Genesis, if one may put it so. ["I'm not sure that one may phrase the resemblance in that way."] [2]
She is resigning, if you know what I mean. [也许 "You are to interpret that to mean that she has been asked to resign."] [3]

在例[1]和[2]中，讲话人对用词正确与否并无把握。例[3]中，讲话人无从肯定听话人是否会正确理解自己的用词，因此告诫对方要按讲话人的本意理解。其他的例子有：

if I may put it so, if that's the correct term, if that's the word for it, if you see what I mean, if I may phrase it delicately /loosely /crudely /figuratively, if you will〈正式用法〉, if you like

虽然带有 I 的分句明确表示讲话人并无把握，但诸如 if I may put it so 之类的分句可以用来更为婉转地表示告诫。

(c) 条件分句表示对正确理解话语所要求的语言外的知识没有把

握。这可能是讲话人没有把握，也可能是听话人没有把握：

I met your girl friend Caroline last night, if Caroline IS your girl friend. [4]
Chomsky's views cannot be reconciled with Piaget's, if I understand both correctly. [5]
The war was started by the other side, if you remember your history lessons. [6]
Einstein's theory of gravitation is based on a mathematical concept, if you've not forgotten already. [7]

例[4]和[5]中的条件分句对讲话人自己知道与否没有表态，而例[6]和

if I'm correct, if I understand you correctly, if we can believe the experts, in case you don't remember, if you remember, if you know what I'm referring to, in case you don't know.

(d) 条件分句表示讲话人赖以发话的条件：

If you're going my way, I need a lift back. ["If you're going my way, will you please give me a lift back."] [8]
In case he ever asks you, I don't know you. ["In case he ever asks you, tell him that I don't know you."] [9]

If you want to borrow a shoebrush, there's one in the bathroom. ["If you want...use the one in the bathroom."] [10]

注意，例[8]和[9]两句话是意在言外的间接请求，例[10]是意在言外的间接提议，例[11]是意在言外的直接提问。间接条件分句表示没有把握。如果讲话人对条件的满足有把握，那末可用 since-分句取代：

Since you're going my way, I need a lift back. [8a]

以上四类条件句的不肯定性使人感到用的是试探口吻，从而增加了话语的礼貌程度。

【注】

除 if 外，用来引导间接条件句的其他从属连词有 in case (that)，assuming (that)，in the event (that) 和 supposing (that)。

##### 让步分句

##### 从属连词和分句的结构类型

15.39 让步分句主要由 although 或其较非正式的变体 though 引导。与让步分句连用的其他从属连词有：

if, even if, even though, when, whereas〈正式用法〉, while, 和 whilst〈尤其在英国英语中〉。

请再参见后面 as 和 that〈英国英语〉的特殊的让步用法。

Although he had just joined the company, he was treated exactly like all the other employees. No goals were scored, though it was an exciting game. While I don't want to make a fuss, I feel I must protest at your interference.
Whereas the amendment is enthusiastically supported by a large majority in the Senate, its fate is doubtful in the House.
She paid when she could have entered free.
He borrowed my mower even though I told him not to.
除 when 和 whereas 之外，让步从属连词可引导-ing，-ed 和动词分句：
While not wanting to seem obstinate, I insisted on a definite reply.
Even though given every opportunity, they would not cooperate with us.
Though well over eighty, he can walk faster than I can.
这几类分句不用从属连词也可表示让步关系，虽然这时为使这种系明确一般要求有一个关联联加状语：
Not wanting to give offence, they did so all the same.

这几类分句不用从属连词也可表示让步关系，虽然这时为使这种关系明确一般要求有一个关联联加状语：

Not wanting to give offence, they did so all the same. Trained in karate, he nevertheless used a gun to de-

fend himself.
Aware of the dangers to American citizens during the crisis, she still insisted on staying with the others.

像条件分句(参见 15.36)一样，当从属连词是 as 或 though时，让步分句有时有异常的句法顺序。在一种相当王式的语体里，让步分句里的谓语可放到句首：

Genius though she was, she was quite unassuming. Fail though I did, I would not abandon my goal. Naked as I was, I braved the storm. ["Even though I was naked,..."]
Change your mind as you will, you will gain no additional support. ["Even though you change your mind,..."]

这样的语序对 though 来说是并非强制性的，但对 as 来说则是强制性的，因为 as 若在句首就不是让步分句了（但参见下面【注】[d]）。

that 也可用在像 as 一样的强制性语序中表示让步，但在美国英语中只有作主语补语的名词短语可以前置：

Fool that he was, he managed to evade his pursuers.
["Even though he was a fool,..."]

这个名词短语具有描述作用(参见10.20)。但是在英国英语中，一个作主语补语的形容词短语也可放到句首：

Poor that they were, they gave money to charity. 《英国英语》[“Even though they were poor,...”]关于状况分句中 as 和 that 的类似倒装语序，参见 15.47。

##### 【注】

[a] 有几个介词短语后面跟一个关系分句也可以表示让步关系：

despite
in spite of
irrespective of
regardless of
notwithstanding
} the fact (that)

由于这些介词短语比从属连词长，因此语体显得臃肿。

[b] 关于作让步连加状语的 though，参见 8.137。

[c] 在诸如 greatly though I admire her 和 much as I would

like to help 的让步分句中，只有副词非放句首不可。这类前置只限于从属连词 though 和 as。

[d] 让步从属连词 as 不放在句首也许和下面那个例子中不常用的让步分句 as...as 有关：

As widespread as the effects may be, the Midwest still bears the brunt of the recession. ["Even though the effects may be widespread,..."]

因此这个不放在句首的 as 可看作是被省略的句首 as 的关联词，另见比较关联词 as...as 中第一个 as 的类似省略(参见 15.71)。

##### 让步关系

15.40 让步分句表示，母句中的情境与由让步分句中所说情形产生的预期情境相反。由于这种相互关系的缘故，哪一个分句作从句常常纯粹是一个选择问题：

No goals were scored, although it was an exciting game.
It was an exciting game, although no goals were scored.

它们常常也隐含两个分句所描写的两种情境之间的对比。

although 和较非正式的 though 是最为通用的从属连词，因为它们实际上可以关联情境相似的分句：

Although Sam had told the children a bedtime story, June told them one too (anyway).

while 和 whilst 就较受限制，但它们可以关联两个差别不大的分句，让步关系由一个与预期相反的情境产生：

While he has many friends, Peter is (nevertheless) often lonely.

While I admit I did it, (nevertheless) I didn't intend to.

whereas 是这四个从属连词中最受限制的一个，它要求两个情境之间有对偶关系：

Whereas it would be naive to maintain that inflation is no longer of concern, (nevertheless) all the economic indicators suggest that the money supply can

now be safely increased.

even though 和 even when 是 though 和 when 更为强调的形式，修饰性 even 也表示出乎意料。但是，even if 把 even 的让步含义和 if 的条件含义结合了起来；因此例[1]和[2]在语义上是有差别的：

Even though you disLIKE ancient monuments, Warwick Castle is worth a visit. [1] Even if you dislike ancient monuments, Warwick Castle is worth a visit. [2]

例 [1] 中 even though 分句以 “you dislike ancient monuments” 为先决条件，而例 [2] 中的 even if 则对这个问题未作肯定。例 [1] 的先决条件可通过加进情态动词 may 或像 perhaps 那样模棱两可的状语来加以消除。

if 本身可以用来表示让步关系：

If he's poor, he's (at least) honest. ["He may be poor, yet he's at least honest."] [3]
If he's poor he's (also) honest. ["He is poor, yet he's also honest."] [3a]
例[3]中，if 被解释为 even if 的同义词，例[3a]中，if 则被解释为 even though. 让步 if 的这两种不同用法常出现在缩略的无动词分词中：
It's possible, if difficult. ["It may be difficult."]
My car is as clean as yours, if not cleaner. ["It may be cleaner."]
He spoke ungraciously, if not rudely. ["He may have spoken rudely."]
They were in good health, if somewhat fatter than desirable. ["They were somewhat fatter than desirable."]
Her salary was good, if not up to her expectations. ["Her salary was not up to her expectations."]

【注】

关于有让步含义的 when，参见 15.29。

##### 选择条件-让步分句

15.41 条件和让步的交叠关系，在论述 even if 时已特别提到（参见 15.40），在称为选择条件-让步（ALTERNATIVE CONDITIONAL-CONCESSIVE）和一般条件-让步（UNIVERSAL CONDITIONAL-CONCESSIVE）的两类状语分句中尤为明显。

关联词组 whether...or (whether) 是一种选择条件，因为从逻辑上说，它把 if 的条件意义和 either...or 的外加状语意义结合在一起（另见【注】[a]. 因此，这是一种把两种从属分句并列的手段。如果第二个单位是个完整的分句，可将 whether 重复，如例[1]；参见 15.6:

Whether Martin pays for the broken vase or (whether) he replaces it with a new vase, I'm not inviting HIM again. [1]
You will have to face the publicity, whether you want to or not. [2]
Whether or not he finds a job, he's getting married. [3]

让步意义来自同一情境适用于两种不同条件的、出人意料的蕴含。例如，例[3]可以释义为“Even if he finds a job or even if he doesn't find a job, he's getting married.”关于例[2]和[3]的选择语序，参见【注】[a]。

较长又较强调的结构 It doesn't matter whether (只放在句首) 和 No matter whether 也可用来引导选择条件-让步分句(参见 15.42)。

You will have to face the publicity, no matter whether you want to or not. [2a]
It doesn't matter whether or not he finds a job, he's getting married. [3a]

这些从属连词也引导非限定分句和无动词分句：

Sarah is always intense, whether working or playing. [4]

Whether trained or not, Marilyn is doing an excellent job. [5]

No matter whether right or wrong, your son needs all the support you can give him right now. [6]

从属连词可予省略，不过，这时分句通常前置于句首：

Working or playing, Sarah is always intense. [4a] Trained or not, Marilyn is doing an excellent job. [5a]

也有些无动词分句用 with 引导，这时 with 和 without 形成关联：

We'll buy the house, with a bank loan or without one. [7]

With or without a bank loan,we'll buy the house. [7a]

如果并列名词短语的第二项由限定词 no 否定，上面这种意思也可只用并列的名词短语表达：

We'll buy the house, bank loan or no bank loan. [8] 当隐含的谓语动词是 be 而不是 have 时，这种结构也适用：

I have to go to work, rain or no rain. ["...whether or not there is rain.] [9]

用省略第二个名词短语来作进一步缩略，虽不太常见，却不是不可能的。这时缩略后的分句通常放在句首：

例[7—10]所列示的各类句子中，无动词分句既可以在句首，也可在句末。例[8—10]所列示的几类句子，具数名词（如bank loan）之前的不定冠词被省略。

##### 【注】

[a] 我们也可见到一种与选择疑问分句(参见 15.6)有联系的关系。试将上述例[1]和下例作比较：

I don't know whether Martin will pay for the broken vase or whether he will replace it, I'm not inviting him again anyway.

例[2]中从属分句的语序可重新排列为 whether or not you want to, 例[3]中从属分句的语序可重新排列为 whether he finds a job or not. 参见 11.20f，选择疑问句。

[b] 偶尔，择选条件-让步意义由一个不带从属连词的限定分句表达，因为谓语动词用了虚拟语气(15.34【注】[d]，15.42【注】[b])：Rain or shine, we're having our party outside today.

["Whether it rains or shines……"]

["Whether it rains or shines,..."]
试比较：(Come) wind or rain ["whether wind or rain comes."] 一种较为罕见而又多少带点文学色彩的结构是用 be 的虚拟式：
(Be he) friend or foe, the law regards him as a criminal. ["Whether he is (or be) friend or foe,..."]

[c] 第二分句中的选择项可能只相应于第一分句的一个部分。因此，相当于例[6]的限定分句便是：
No matter whether he's right or wrong,...
而例[5]稍作修改就会是：
Whether trained as a nurse or as a radiologist...

[d] 有些人用 either（参见 13.39ff）时，容许有两个以上的选择项（参见 15.6【注】【b】）：
Whether you do your homework or play or watch television, you must not disturb me.

[e] 类似 no matter whether 形式的还有 regardless of whether 和 irrespective of whether (参见 15.39【注】[a]):
Regardless of whether or not he finds a job, he's getting married.

##### 一般条件-让步分句

15.42 选择分句和一般分句之间的区别类似于选择疑问句(参见11.20f)和wh-疑问句(参见11.14ff)之间的区别，也类似于它们相应的从属分句(参见15.5f)之间的区别。选择条件-让步分句要求在已阐明的，一般是绝然相反的两个(偶尔两个以上，参见15.41【注】【d】)的条件中进行选择，而一般条件-让步分句则表示可以从任何数量的条件中自由选择。试比较：

Whether I shout at them or plead with them, I can't keep them quiet. [所述两种情况的选择] [1] Whatever I say to them, I can't keep them quiet. [多种情况的选择] [2]

例[2]中的让步含义来自如下推理：即使我答应款待他们，我还是不能

使他们安静下来。

选择分句由 wh- 词+ever 构成的复合词及 It doesn't matter （只用于句首）和 No matter（参见 15.41）+wh-成分构成的较长结构引导。这些分句与其他 wh-分句一样，wh-成分放在首位，因而（除非是主语）就离开了它正常的句法位置：

Stand perfectly still, wherever you are. [ASV]
However much advice you give him, he does exactly
what he wants.  $ [O_{d}SVO_{i}] $

Don't let them in, whoever they are. [CₛSV]

在一般条件-让步分句和以 whenever 和 wherever 开头的，显然完全相同的时间及地点分句之间有一种微妙的语义差别。这种语义差别可从下面这样一个句子中显示出来：

Wherever you live, you can keep a horse.
作地点分句解时，它的意思是：“You can keep a horse at any place where you may live.”(参见特定地点 where: You can keep a horse where you live.) 作条件-让步分句解时，它的意思(更适用于城市居民)是：“It doesn't matter where you live, you can keep a horse (and the horse need not be in the same place as you live).”

##### 【注】

[a] 如果 SVC 分句的主语是一个抽象名词短语，一般条件-让步分句中的谓语动词 be 可以省略：

Whatever your problems (are/may be), they can't be worse than mine.

However great the pitfalls (are/may be), we must do our best to succeed.

[b] 偶尔，一般条件-让步分句可由一个不带从属连词的限定分句表达，在此情况下，其谓语动词用虚拟语气而且放在句首（参见10.34【注】[d]，15.41【注】【b】）：Come what may ["Whatever may happen."]，Be that as it may ["However that may be."]

##### 对比分句

15.43 对比分句由若干引导让步分句(参见 15.39)的从属连词引导：whereas，while 和 whilst，实际上，对比和让步常常混在一起。当对比分句放在句首时，其对比意义可用诸如 in contrast 和 by contrast 等关联对偶联加状语来强调：

Mr Larson teaches physics, while Mr Corby teaches chemistry.
I ignore them, whereas my husband is always worried about what they think of us.

这三个从属连词是相互通用的，只是不常见的 whilst 特别在英国英语中屡有所见。

##### 例外分句

对比分句与用 but 并列的分句十分相似。当对比分句放在句末时尤其如此。当对比分句出现在句首时，就被看作含有从属的信息，即对比的出发点。

15.44 例外分句由若干从属连词引导：but that〈正式用法〉，except (that)；不太常见的有 excepting (that) 和 save that 〈正式用法〉。有几个从属连词也同时表示例外和条件。除对 save that 语体上有限制外，except (that)，excepting (that) 和 save that 的用法十分相似：

I would pay you now, except I don't have any money on me.
No memorial remains for the brave who fell on that battlefield, save that they will leave their image for ever in the hearts and minds of their grateful countrymen.〈正式用法〉

像介词 but 一样，but that 要求母句位于其前并且是否定句：

Nothing would satisfy the child but that I place her on my lap.〈正式用法〉 [1]

而且更常见的是用一个不定式分句：

Nothing would satisfy the child but for me to place her on my lap. [1]

在固定的句子中，可以只出现 but:

It never rains but it pours.

only 限于非正式语体，也表示例外的意思（参见下面【注】[a]）：

I would've asked you, only my mother told me not to. unless 同时表示条件和例外（“except if”），因此有否定意义；proviæed (that) 及其同义词都是肯定意义的对应词。

关于引导无 to 和有 to 不定式分句的具有例外意义的介词，参见 9.58。

##### 【注】

[a] only 是一个介于联加状语和连词之间的词。是否可在两个分句中间插入一个并列连词（比如 but），这个问题并不清楚；如果可以插入，only 就具有这类联加状语的一个特征（参见 8.134ff）；如果不能插入，则 only 的句法地位就与 for 相似，因为在递差度上，for 介于并列连词和从属连词之间（参见 13.18f）。only 可释义为 “The only thing is”.

[b] except (that), excepting (that) 和 save that 通常可用并列连词 but 取代。它们通常可用“介词短语+关系分句”——例如 except for/apart from the fact (that)——取代，但因较长而显得臃肿。凡是不能用连词和介词短语取代的语境，便是允许用 but that 的地方。

[c] 在美国英语中，例 [1] 从属分句中的谓语动词多用现在时虚拟语气，而英国英语中则多用推定意义的 should（参见 14.24f）。

##### 原因分句

##### 直接和间接原因关系

15.45 我们把几类与母句关系基本相似的从属分句归入原因(REASON)分句。就所有这些类型而言，一般都有一个从属分句情境在时间上先于母句情境的时间顺序。如下列释义句所示，reason这个词是一个适用于所有各类的上义词。

(a) 原因与效果：本结构表示人们认识到现实世界中的一种固有

的客观联系：

The flowers are growing so well because I sprayed them. ["The cause for the flowers growing so well is that I sprayed them" 或 "The reason that the flowers are growing so well is that I sprayed them."] He's thin because he doesn't eat enough.

(b) 前因与后果：本结构表示讲话人对一种联系的推论：

She watered the flowers because they were dry. [“The reason that she watered the flowers was that they were dry.”]

Since she's my friend, she must have put in a good word for me.

(c) 动机与效果：本结构表示有效果的有生物的意图：

I watered the flowers because my parents told me to do so. ["My motivation for watering the flowers was that my parents told me to do so" 或 "The reason that I watered the flowers was that my parents told me to do so."]

You'll help me because you're my friend.

动机总是包括能动作用和意图的。

(d) 状况与后果：状况分句同时表示原因和认为要实现或将实现的一种条件，本结构表示从属分句中的前提和母句中结论之间的一种关系：

Since the weather has improved, the game will be held as planned. ["In view of the fact that the weather has improved, the game will be held as planned" or "The reason that the game will be held as planned is that the weather has improved."]

Seeing that it is only three, we should be able to finish this before we leave today.

上列例句表示原因分句和母句之间的一种直接原因(DIRECT REASON)关系。原因分句较为扩展的用法是表示一种间接原因(INDIRECT REASON)。这个原因与母句中的情境无关而表示该话语言语行为的一个含蓄的动机：

Percy is in Washington, for he phoned me from there.

["Since he phoned from there, I can tell you that Percy is in Washington."]
As you're in charge, where are the files on the new project? ["As you're in charge, I'm asking you...?"] Vanessa is your favourite aunt, because your parents told me so. ["Since your parents told me so, I can say that Vanessa is your favourite aunt."]
As long as you're here, why don't we discuss our plans?
Since you seem to know them, why don't you introduce me to them? ["Since you seem to know them, I ask you to introduce me to them."]

since 和 because 是表示间接原因最常用的从属连词。表示间接原因的分句均是语体外加状语，参见 15.21。

##### 从属连词和分句的结构类型

15.46 最常用来引导原因分句的从属连词是 because (也有 cause) 和 since。其他从属连词有 as 和 (在多少正式的语体里) for:

(cause)和since。其他从属连词有as和(在多少正式的语体里)for: I lent him the money because he needed it. As Jane was the eldest, she looked after the others. Since we live near the sea, we often go sailing. Much has been written about psychic phenomena, for they pose fascinating problems that have yet to be resolved.
in case 同时表示原因和可能 ("because it may happen that"):
Take your umbrella in case it rains. ["Take your umbrella because it may rain," "...because of the possibility that it will rain."]
You should write a will in case something happens to you abroad.
引导状况分句（参见15.45）的有简单从属连词（如 because, since 和 as）以及几个复杂从属连词（如 seeing (that), as long as, inasmuch as〈正式用法〉）:

Seeing that it seems as if it will rain soon, we had

better leave now.

As long as you're here, we might as well talk about your last game.

It is doubtful whether research proposals by Freud himself would have been approved by reviewers, inasmuch as he was not affiliated to any academic institution.〈正式用法〉

用 with 引导的分句也可以是状况分句：

With the exams coming next week, I have no time for a social life.
With so many children to support, they both have to work full time.

再参见 15.28 状况从属连词 now (that).

in that〈正式用法〉同时表示原因和观点：
The evidence is invalid in that it was obtained through illegal means. ["The evidence is invalid in this respect: it was obtained through illegal means."]〈正式用法〉

While 引导一个语体外加状语时，既表示时间又表示原因：
While you're in the kitchen, bring me another drink.
无从属连词的分句可能隐含本节所讨论的含义：
Knowing their tastes, she was able to bring a gift that they would like.
Constructed according to my specifications, the building was able to withstand the earthquake.
Assured of your support, he would not compromise.

as 和 since 既是时间连词，又是原因连词，这一现象证明原因和时间序列有着密切而又明显的联系。但这一双重功能可能产生歧义：

As he was standing near the door, he could hear the conversation in the kitchen. ["Since he was standing near the door..." 或 "While he was standing near the door..."]

##### 【注】

[a] 许多介词短语用来引导原因关系，但因其冗长而语体常显得臃肿：

because of

by virtue of

in (the) light of

in view of

on account of

owing to

due to

{the fact (that)

关于规定语法反对把 due to 用作介词，参见 15.59【注】【d】，关于 no account of 在非正式语体中（尤其在美国英语中）用作从属连词，参见 14.12【注】【e】。

[b] 不定式分句可以表述一个近似于 in that 表述的原因：

He's foolish to make such a fuss. [“…in that he makes such a fuss.”]

不定式分句也可同时表示原因和条件，参见15.34[注][g].

[c] 固定的分句 come to think of it, 没有从属连词而且谓语动词用原形，义同 now that I come to think of it:

Come to think of it, shouldn't you write to her?

[d] in case 的原因/条件含义容易成为一个否定目的含义(参见15.35[注][g]，15.48).试比较：

Write a will in case you die. ["...because you may die."]

Write a will in case you die without providing for your family. ["...because you may die without providing for your family," "in order that you do not die without providing for your family"]

[e] 表示状况的 what with 指一组非特定的已知状况中的一个或几个，而表示状况的 with 仅指一种状况：

What with the prices (being) so high, (and (with) my wife being out of work), I can't afford a new refrigerator.

请注意，如不出现并列的 and (with)...就可能加上一个非正式语体的 and all:

What with Carol (being) out of work and all, we

有一个完全对应的固定短语：
What with one thing and another, I couldn't sleep last night.
[i] as+名词短语可相当于一个限定分句：
As I'm your mother, I'll decide.
As your mother,
[g] 当 because 分句是附加状语而非语体外加状语时，它相当于一个由 because of 引导的介词短语：
The flowers are growing well because I fertilized them.
them.
[h] because-分句有时非正式地当 that-分句使用：
(Just) because I object to his promotion doesn't mean that I'm vindictive. ["The (mere) fact that I object..."]
[1]
规定语法反对这种用法。其他说法有：
My objection to his promotion doesn't mean that My objecting I'm vindictive.
[1a]
I can't be accused of being vindictive (just) because I object to his promotion.
[1b]
规定语法也反对和前面 why 或 the reason (that)关联的 because-分句的非正式用法，斥之为冗余。
Why
The reason (that) they didn't go to see the house is because they prefer to live in an apartment.
[2]
规定语法同样反对用 the reason why 来代替 the reason that. 用 that 替代 because 之后，例[2]便完全可以接受。

15.47 大多数用来表示直接原因的从属连词引导内容外加状语但是 because，in case 和 in that 引导附加状语(参见 15.20)。

作附加状语的 because-分句往往位于句首，而作语体外加状语的 because-分句总是位于句末。for 接近于并列连词，总是位于句末。伦敦-隆德口语语料库（它拥有“英语用法调查”的大部分口头语篇）
